# ReelForge: full documentation for language models

> Generated by scripts/gen-llms.mjs from 39 files. The short index is llms.txt.

<!-- file: AGENTS.md -->

# AGENTS.md — ReelForge for AI agents

This file is for AI coding agents and assistants (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini
CLI, Windsurf, Aider, Zed, Jules, …). It has two parts. **Part 1** covers making videos with
ReelForge, which is what most people ask for. **Part 2** covers changing the ReelForge source code.

ReelForge turns **a voice recording + one `episode.yaml`** into a finished **1080×1920 vertical
explainer video** for TikTok, Reels and Shorts. Everything runs locally. There is no AI in
the render engine; speech alignment and scene suggestions are optional local helpers
(`reelforge align --setup` downloads the speech models once, then everything runs offline). The same
inputs always produce the same frames.

---

## Part 1 · Making videos

### Prefer the MCP server

If your client supports the Model Context Protocol, use the `reelforge` MCP server. It is already
configured for this project in `.mcp.json` (Claude Code), `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json` and
`.gemini/settings.json`. Start it with:

```bash
node packages/cli/bin/reelforge.js mcp      # or: ./reelforge mcp · reelforge.cmd mcp
```

| Tool                                                     | Use it to                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list_episodes`                                          | see what exists                                                              |
| `get_episode`                                            | read episode.yaml plus a compiled outline (line times, element paths, boxes) |
| `list_templates` / `create_from_template`                | industry templates; make an episode by filling a few flat slots (easiest)    |
| `create_episode`                                         | start a new episode from a script (draft cues are written for you)           |
| `suggest_scenes`                                         | a scene plan for every line: a blueprint and the best single element         |
| `list_blueprints` / `add_scene`                          | add a whole scene (hook, stat-reveal, comparison, steps…) from parameters    |
| `edit_episode`                                           | structured edits (`set` / `delete` / `insert` / `move` by YAML path)         |
| `write_episode_yaml`                                     | replace the whole file (validated before writing)                            |
| `validate_episode`                                       | run all checks (V-1…V-14) with line numbers and fix hints                    |
| `preview_frames`                                         | **look** at frames (returned as images); always check your work              |
| `list_components` / `get_component_schema`               | the 62 components and their exact props                                      |
| `suggest_scene`                                          | element ideas for a line (component, props, enter word); optional local LLM  |
| `draft_cues` / `set_cues`                                | estimated or known line timings                                              |
| `align_cues`                                             | cues for every line and word, aligned automatically to `voice.wav`           |
| `render_episode` / `get_render_status` / `cancel_render` | render in the background, poll, cancel                                       |
| `open_editor`                                            | give the person a URL to the visual editor to fine-tune and mark cues        |
| `doctor`                                                 | check Node.js, FFmpeg, Chromium and fonts                                    |
| `get_guide`                                              | task guides from `skills/` (short by default, `detail: true` for all of it)  |

**Pick the tools for your model size.** Small models: `list_templates` → `create_from_template` →
`validate_episode`. Medium models: `create_episode` → `suggest_scenes` → `add_scene`. Strong models:
`edit_episode` / `write_episode_yaml` for free composition. Guide: `get_guide` `reelforge-make-video`.

Every write tool (`create_from_template`, `add_scene`, `create_episode`, `edit_episode`, `write_episode_yaml`, `set_cues`, `draft_cues`,
`align_cues`) returns the validation summary, `fixes` (one hint per problem) and `next` (the
recommended next step). `preview_frames` returns a text layout description per frame (boxes,
overlaps, platform UI zones) next to each image.

**Other ways in.** The same tools are served by `reelforge studio` (the dashboard, default
`http://127.0.0.1:4310`): MCP Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, and a REST API at `/api/v1`
(`GET /api/v1/tools`, `POST /api/v1/tools/<name>` with the arguments as JSON,
`GET /api/v1/openapi.json` for OpenAI-compatible function calling and GPT Actions). The dashboard's
**Connect AI** page (`/connect`) has copy-paste setup for each client; `/.well-known/mcp.json`
describes the server and `/llms-full.txt` has the docs in one file. Ask for fewer tools with
toolsets: `reelforge mcp --toolsets basic,design` or `/mcp?toolsets=basic` (`basic`, `design`,
`render`, `all`). Tool names and arguments follow semver (ADR-014).

Without MCP, use the command line (`./reelforge` on macOS/Linux, `reelforge.cmd` on Windows):

```bash
./reelforge new ep10 --lang en --series "SYSTEM DESIGN"   # episodes/ep10/episode.yaml
./reelforge cue ep10 --draft                              # estimated cues (no recording yet)
./reelforge align ep10                                    # cues from voice.wav (lines + words)
./reelforge validate ep10 --json                          # machine-readable issues
./reelforge snap ep10 l1+1 "l3:'bucket'" --out /tmp/f     # PNG frames to look at
./reelforge render ep10 --silent --json                   # render without a voice
./reelforge edit ep10                                     # visual editor for the human
```

### Skills

Task guides live in `skills/` (Agent Skills format: one folder per skill with `SKILL.md` and
`references/`): `reelforge-make-video`, `reelforge-script-writing`, `reelforge-scene-design`,
`reelforge-timing`, `reelforge-brand-and-themes`, `reelforge-industry-playbooks`,
`reelforge-review-and-render` and `reelforge-contribute-component`. Read them as files, or call
`get_guide` (`topic`, `detail: true` for the full guide, `"<topic>/<reference>"` for a reference).
`.claude-plugin/` packages them with the MCP server as a Claude Code plugin.

### Workflow that works

1. **Script first.** Write one short spoken sentence per line, about 2.3 words per second. Line 1
   is the hook (a question or a surprising fact). Introduce one idea per line. The last line is a
   call to action. 45 seconds is about 100–110 words.
2. **Create** the episode, using `create_episode` with the script or `reelforge new`.
3. **Design scenes.** Put one idea in each scene, usually 4–7 scenes in an episode. Each scene
   starts on a line (`at: l3`). Make each element enter **on the word that names it**, for example
   `enter: { at: "l3:'bucket'" }`. This word-sync is what makes ReelForge videos feel alive.
   `suggest_scene` gives a valid starting point per line (component, props, enter word).
4. **Validate** and fix every error and warning. V-14 flags lines spoken faster than ~3.5 words/s
   (too fast to read in captions) and a hook that starts after 3 s.
5. **Preview** frames shortly after things enter (`l3:'bucket'+0.8`). Check overlap, text overflow
   and that the platform UI is clear. Iterate until it looks clean.
6. **Hand over.** The person records `voice.wav`. `align_cues` (or `reelforge align`) marks every
   line and word from the recording; the person listens through once in the editor (Cues mode) and
   fixes any line by ear, then renders. Until then the draft cues give realistic timing. Phone
   recordings: set `audio: { denoise: true }` to remove background noise when rendering.

### episode.yaml essentials

```yaml
meta:
  id: ep10
  series: 'SYSTEM DESIGN'
  title: 'Rate Limiting'
  episode: 10
  preset: tiktok # tiktok | reels | shorts
  theme: default # default | season1 | workshop (or your own)
  lang: en-US # en-US → left-to-right captions; ar-EG → right-to-left
  publish: { cover: 'Flooded API?', caption: '…', hashtags: ['#systemdesign'], pinned: '…' }

audio: { voice: voice.wav, sfx: auto, sfx_gain_db: -16 } # denoise: true for noisy recordings

script: # ids default to l1, l2, … by position
  - text: 'Your API just got flooded with requests.'
  - text: 'A rate limiter decides who gets through.'

chapters:
  - { at: l1, label: '01 · THE PROBLEM' }

scenes:
  - id: hook
    at: l1 # starts with line 1; ends where the next scene starts
    glow: red # background glow: lime cyan red amber violet ink …
    elements:
      - use: title
        id: hook_title
        props: { text: 'Flooded **API**' } # **word** = accent color
        place: { x: 60, y: 160, w: 960, h: 240 }
        enter: { at: "l1:'flooded'", anim: pop }
      - use: counter
        id: rps
        props: { from: 0, keyframes: [{ at: "l1:'requests'", value: 12000, dur: 1.2 }], suffix: ' req/s' }
        place: { x: 140, y: 460, w: 800, h: 300 }
        enter: { at: "l1:'requests'", anim: rise }
```

**Time expressions:** `12.5s`, `l7` (line start), `l7.end`, `l7:'word'`, `l7:'word'#2` (second
match), `l7.3` (4th word, 0-based), `@scene`, `@scene.end`, plus offsets such as `+0.4` or `-0.2`.
Quote YAML strings that contain `:` or `'`, e.g. `at: "l3:'bucket'"`.

**Layout:** all coordinates are **stage coordinates**: 1080 wide × 1000 high, with the origin at
the top-left of the stage. The stage spans canvas y 270–1270 and the captions sit below it. Rules:

- Keep a 60 px side margin: `x ≥ 60` and `x + w ≤ 1020`.
- In the lower part of the stage (y > 600), keep `x + w ≤ 920`. The TikTok right rail (likes,
  comments) covers the canvas from x 940 down.
- Don't let two visible base elements overlap (V-8). Use `exit` to clear space, or `layer: overlay`
  for stamps and badges that should sit on top.
- Big readable text: titles 80–130 px, body 36–56 px. Don't put more than about 7 words in a
  title.

**Animation:** `enter.anim`: pop (default), rise, slide-l, slide-r, fade, draw, type, count, flip,
zoom, glitch, stamp, blur, wipe, spring, drop, reveal, none. `enter.ease`: smooth (default), snappy,
gentle, linear. `exit: { at, anim }`: fade, pop, rise, sink, slide-l, slide-r, zoom, blur, wipe.
Scenes: `transition`: crossfade (default), cut, slide-up, zoom, push, blur; `camera`: still, drift,
push-in, pull-out. Use `reveal` for big titles, `spring`/`pop` for chips, a `push` or `zoom`
transition between chapters, and vary them; the same animation everywhere looks mechanical.
`fx: [{ at, do: shake|flash|glitch|pulse|bump }]` (`target: camera` shakes the whole frame).
`states: [{ at, set: { status: err } }]` changes props over time.

**Components (62):**

- Text: title, label, chip, stamp, quote, kinetic-text, bullet-list, speech-bubble.
- Diagrams: node, arrow (`from`/`to` = element ids such as `api.left`, or points), lanes, grid,
  timeline, bucket, callout (label + arrow pointing at an element), spotlight (dims all but one
  element).
- Data & charts: counter, meter (`style: gauge`), table, checklist, bar-chart, line-chart,
  donut-chart, stat-card, progress-ring, comparison, before-after, ranking, vitals (ECG + BPM).
- Structure: steps, flow, org-chart, tree, cycle, funnel, pyramid, matrix-2x2.
- Places: map (countries, pins, routes), route (moving vehicle), floor-plan, building,
  container-stack.
- Time & people: calendar, clock (`mode: countdown`), schedule-board, appointment, person-card,
  chat, notification, lower-third.
- Media & commerce: image (Ken Burns), logo, split-screen, pricing-table (`variant: tag`),
  qr-code, rating (illustrative only).
- Other: code (types itself), phone, icon (~250 bundled icons), particles, trap ("THE TRAP"
  interstitial), cta (next-episode ending).

Ask `get_component_schema` (or read `docs/components.md`) before using a component's props; props
are strict.

### Quality checklist (do all of these before you say "done")

- [ ] `validate_episode` shows **0 errors**. Warnings are fixed or explained to the person.
- [ ] Every scene has something entering within its first 1.5 s.
- [ ] Each element enters on a word it relates to. Nothing appears "randomly".
- [ ] Preview frames are clean: no overflow, no overlap, nothing under the platform UI.
- [ ] Arabic episodes keep technical terms in English inside the Arabic sentence (`الـ client`).
      Captions handle the direction automatically.
- [ ] `publish` (cover, caption, hashtags, pinned comment) is filled in.

### Don'ts

- Don't invent component names or props. Use the schemas.
- Don't write absolute seconds when a word expression exists. Words survive re-recording.
- Don't edit `cues.json` by hand unless asked. Use `align_cues` with a recording, or let the person
  mark cues by ear in the editor. `align_cues` never replaces hand-marked cues unless `force: true`.
- Don't delete the person's files under `out/`. Re-rendering overwrites them.
- Rendering takes minutes. Start it and poll; don't block on it.

---

## Part 2 · Working on the ReelForge code

**Stack:** TypeScript 5.9 strict, Node 22, a pnpm 10 workspace, Playwright Chromium for rendering,
FFmpeg as an external binary, Vite for the browser clients and Vitest for tests.

```
packages/
  audio/     WAV I/O, envelopes, onset detection, procedural SFX
  core/      schema (zod), time expressions, captions, themes, presets, compiler → Timeline, lint,
             auto cues (DSP), keyword smart insert
  assist/    optional helpers: cue alignment (DSP / Whisper + Silero VAD, models installed on
             demand into the user cache), scene suggestions from any OpenAI-compatible,
             Anthropic or Ollama model (providers.ts)
  runtime/   browser page: pure render(t) for every component (DOM/SVG)
  renderer/  Chromium workers → x264 segments → concat, loudness, ffprobe checks, doctor
  studio/    local servers: dashboard (hub), editor/cue/review studio; Vite clients in client/;
             the tool registry (src/tools/) behind MCP stdio, MCP HTTP (/mcp) and REST (/api/v1)
  cli/       the `reelforge` command and the MCP stdio transport (src/mcp.ts)
```

- The compiled **Timeline** (`packages/core/src/types.ts`) is the only contract between the
  compiler and the runtime.
- `render(t)` must stay **pure and deterministic**: no `Date.now()`, no unseeded randomness and no
  timers in the runtime.
- Local servers bind to **127.0.0.1**, check Host/Origin and accept JSON-only writes. Keep it that
  way. Only the dashboard may bind elsewhere (`--host`), and then a bearer token guards `/mcp` and
  `/api/v1` (ADR-015).
- The editor writes `episode.yaml` through structured operations
  (`packages/studio/src/server/edit.ts`), which keeps comments.
- AI tools live in one registry (`packages/studio/src/tools/`, ADR-014). To add one, define it with
  `defineTool` in a group file (Zod input, toolsets, annotations, handler) and list the group in
  `registry.ts`; MCP, REST, the OpenAPI document and the server card pick it up.

**Commands:**

```bash
pnpm install && pnpm build
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint
pnpm test:unit          # fast
REELFORGE_TEST_MODELS=1 pnpm test:unit   # + real Whisper / Ollama (after `reelforge align --setup`)
node scripts/eval-assist.mjs             # cue accuracy and speed against ground truth
pnpm test               # + browser/integration (needs FFmpeg and Chromium)
pnpm format             # prettier
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 pnpm test:browser   # refresh golden frames after an intended visual change
```

**Adding a component:**

1. Add its schema and defaults in `packages/core/src/components/`.
2. Add its runtime in `packages/runtime/src/components/`.
3. Add it to the gallery in `fixtures/golden/components/episode.yaml`.
4. Regenerate `docs/components.md` with `node scripts/gen-components-doc.mjs`.
5. Refresh the golden frames.

**Conventions:**

- Match the surrounding style.
- Write comments only where the code can't say it.
- Keep user-facing text in clear English.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass.

---

<!-- file: docs/authoring.md -->

# Authoring guide

Everything about an episode lives in `episodes/<id>/`:

```
episodes/ep10/
  episode.yaml   the spec (you write this)
  voice.wav      your recording (any sample rate, mono or stereo; other formats are converted with ffmpeg)
  cues.json      line and word start times (written by `reelforge align`, Cues mode or `reelforge cue --draft`)
  assets/        optional images/SVGs referenced as assets/<file>
  out/           generated: master, share, SRT, contact sheet, publish.md
```

## 1. The spec at a glance

```yaml
meta:
  id: ep10 # slug
  series: 'SYSTEM DESIGN' # header text
  title: 'Idempotency'
  episode: 10
  preset: tiktok # tiktok | reels | shorts (presets/*.preset.yaml)
  theme: season1 # themes/<name>.theme.yaml, or a relative path
  lang: en-US # en-US (left to right) · ar-EG (right to left, English terms supported)
  publish: { cover: '…', caption: '…', hashtags: ['#systemdesign'], pinned: '…' }

audio:
  voice: voice.wav
  sfx: auto # auto | none | manual (only audio.extra and element sfx lists)
  sfx_gain_db: -16
  duck: true # duck SFX under the voice
  denoise: false # true removes background noise from the voice (phone recordings)
  extra: [{ at: "l9:'boom'", sound: hit, gain_db: -3 }]

script: # one spoken sentence per line; ids default to l1, l2, …
  - text: 'Ever paid online and your connection dropped?'
  - id: twice
    text: 'And you got charged twice.'
    break: ['twice'] # force a caption break before this word
    caption: auto # auto | none | "custom caption text"

chapters:
  - { at: l1, label: '01 · THE PROBLEM' }

scenes:
  - id: hook
    at: l1 # start; end defaults to the next scene's start
    glow: red # or a list: [{ at: l1, color: red }, { at: l3, color: lime }]
    transition: crossfade # crossfade | cut | slide-up | zoom | push | blur
    camera: still # still | drift | push-in | pull-out
    layout: stage # stage (between header and captions) | full (whole canvas)
    elements:
      - use: phone
        id: phone
        props: { title: 'Checkout', amount: '$49.00' }
        place: { x: 320, y: 30, w: 440, h: 880 }
        enter: { at: l1, anim: rise, dur: 0.6 }
        exit: { at: l3, anim: fade }
        states:
          - { at: "l1:'dropped'", set: { offline: true } }
        fx:
          - { at: "twice:'twice'", do: shake, amp: 22 }
          - { at: "twice:'twice'", do: flash, color: red }
```

The [episode format reference](reference/episode-format.md) lists every key with its type and default.

## 2. Time expressions

| Form                              | Meaning                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `12.5s` (or a YAML number `12.5`) | absolute seconds                                                            |
| `l7`                              | cue start of line `l7`                                                      |
| `l7.end`                          | start of the next line − 0.15 s                                             |
| `l7:'timeout'`                    | first word matching "timeout" (punctuation, tatweel and diacritics ignored) |
| `l7:'request'#2`                  | second match                                                                |
| `l7:"Conway's"`                   | use double quotes when the word contains `'`                                |
| `l7:'Duplicate Charge'`           | a multi-word phrase (time of its first word)                                |
| `l7.3`                            | the 4th word (0-based)                                                      |
| `@hook`, `@hook.end`              | a scene's start / end                                                       |
| any of the above `+0.4` / `-0.2`  | offset in seconds                                                           |

Word times come from your manual word marks (Cues mode, word mode) or from automatic alignment, or are
estimated by letter count within the line. Every expression is validated; errors name the closest valid alternative. In the
editor you rarely type these: the **target** button and timeline snapping write them for you.

Arabic works the same way: `l7:'مرتين'` anchors to an Arabic word, and English terms inside Arabic
sentences (`الـ client`) are matched as written.

## 3. Placing elements

Stage coordinates: 1080 wide × 1000 high, origin at the top-left of the stage (canvas y = 270 for TikTok).

- `place: { x, y, w, h }` — explicit box (integers)
- `place: { center: true, w, h }` — centered
- `place: { anchor: top|bottom|left|right|center, w, h, margin }`
- no `place` → centered at the component's default size, or laid out by a scene helper:
  - `row: { gap, align, y, h }` — elements side by side
  - `column: { gap, align, x, w }` — stacked
  - `columns: 2` (+ `gutter`, element `col: 0|1`) — lanes
- `size: { w, h }` overrides the default size inside helpers.
- `layer: overlay` puts an element on top and exempts it from the overlap rule (V-8).

Keep content out of the platform UI: the editor's **Z** overlay shows the safe zones of the preset. Keep a
60 px side margin (`x ≥ 60` and `x + w ≤ 1020`), and in the lower part of the stage (y > 600) keep
`x + w ≤ 920`, because the TikTok button rail covers the frame from x = 940. In the editor you can simply
drag and resize elements; it writes `place` for you.

## 4. Animations

`enter.anim`: `pop` (default), `rise`, `slide-l`, `slide-r`, `fade`, `draw`, `type`, `count`, `flip`,
`zoom`, `glitch`, `stamp`, `blur`, `wipe`, `spring`, `drop`, `reveal`, `none`. Parameters: `dur`,
`s0`, `dy`, `dist`, `cps`, `caret`, `rot`, `amp`, `ease`.

| Enter    | Looks like                                                     | Good for                  |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `pop`    | scales up with a small overshoot                               | chips, icons, stamps      |
| `rise`   | fades in while moving up (`dist`, default 40 px)               | cards, code, diagrams     |
| `blur`   | comes into focus from a soft blur                              | calm titles, quotes       |
| `wipe`   | revealed from the start edge (right edge in Arabic)            | timelines, meters, labels |
| `spring` | scales up with a springy settle                                | playful callouts          |
| `drop`   | falls in from above and bounces to rest                        | badges, "result" nodes    |
| `reveal` | slides up out of an invisible mask, like a title card (`dist`) | big titles                |
| `type`   | types character by character (`cps`)                           | code, terminal text       |

`enter.ease` changes how the motion accelerates: `smooth` (default, ease-out), `snappy` (fast
start, long settle), `gentle` (ease-in and out) or `linear`. `pop` and `spring` keep their own
bounce.

`exit.anim`: `fade`, `pop`, `rise`, `sink`, `slide-l`, `slide-r`, `zoom`, `blur`, `wipe`, `none`.

Scene `transition` (how the scene replaces the previous one): `crossfade` (default), `cut`,
`slide-up`, `zoom` (zooms through), `push` (pushes the previous scene off sideways) and `blur`
(soft dissolve). Scene `camera` adds one slow, continuous move across the whole scene: `drift`,
`push-in` (slow zoom in) or `pull-out`. Moves are eased at both ends, so they never jolt.

All motion is rendered with sub-pixel precision, so slow movements stay smooth instead of stepping
one pixel at a time. In the editor, the inspector's **Preview animation** button (and choosing a
new animation, ease or transition) plays just that moment once.

`fx[].do`: `shake` (`target: camera` shakes the whole stage), `flash` (full-frame color hit),
`glitch`, `pulse` (`rate`), `bump`. Flashes add a `hit` sound and glitches a `glitch` sound unless
`sound: none`.

States: `states: [{ at, set: { … } }]` — each component documents the keys it reacts to
(for example `node.status`, `phone.offline`, `chip.strike`, `grid.tiles`). See the [components reference](reference/components.md).

## 5. Sound effects

With `audio.sfx: auto` components emit their default sounds (title → whoosh, stamp → hit, table row → ding,
lane step → tick, …). Disable per element with `sfx: none`, or give a list
`sfx: [{ at: l4, sound: ding }]`. Sounds: `whoosh hit ding err glitch tick tap typing`. Events of the
same sound closer than 80 ms are merged.

## 6. Themes and presets

Themes (`themes/*.theme.yaml`) hold every color, font, size and motion token and can `extends:`
another theme. `chrome.grain_fps` (default 0, a static texture) controls how often the film grain
changes; animated grain multiplies the file size (see ADR-011). Presets (`presets/*.preset.yaml`) hold the canvas, header/stage/caption positions,
safe-zone rectangles, share size and maximum duration — edit them without touching code. See
[Themes and branding](guide/themes.md).

## 7. Validation rules

| Rule | Level | Meaning                                                |
| ---- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| V-1  | error | schema violation (with did-you-mean)                   |
| V-2  | error | unresolvable time expression                           |
| V-3  | error | missing/out-of-order cues                              |
| V-4  | warn  | voice changed since cues were marked, or voice missing |
| V-5  | error | exit before enter, or enter outside the scene          |
| V-6  | warn  | element box outside the stage/canvas                   |
| V-7  | warn  | element in a platform UI zone                          |
| V-8  | warn  | two visible base elements overlap > 15%                |
| V-9  | warn  | text overflows its box (headless measurement)          |
| V-10 | warn  | caption wraps over `max_lines`                         |
| V-11 | info  | nothing enters in a scene's first 1.5 s                |
| V-12 | warn  | element enters < 0.1 s before its scene ends           |
| V-13 | error | unknown component or font                              |
| V-14 | warn  | line spoken > 3.5 words/s, or hook starts after 3 s    |
| V-14 | info  | silence of 1.5 s or more in the recording              |

`reelforge validate <id> --strict` fails on warnings too (use it in CI).

---

<!-- file: docs/components.md -->

# Component reference

Generated from the schemas in `packages/core/src/components/schemas.ts` by
`node scripts/gen-components-doc.mjs`. Props are strict: unknown keys are errors with a
"did you mean" hint.

Conventions:

- Keys named `at` and `until` (at any depth), and `strike`/`highlight` when not booleans, are
  **time expressions**: `12.5s`, `l7`, `l7+0.4`, `l7.end`, `l7:'word'`, `l7:'word'#2`, `l7.3`, `@scene.end`.
- Keys named `color`, `accent`, `danger` and `colors[]` take a **theme color name**
  (`lime`, `cyan`, `red`, `amber`, `violet`, `ink`, `dim`, …) or a CSS color.
- `from`/`to` endpoints are an element id (`api`), an element side (`api.left|right|top|bottom|center`)
  or a point `{x, y}` in stage coordinates.
- Every element also takes the common keys: `id, place, size, col, layer, z, enter, exit, states, fx, sfx`
  (see [authoring.md](authoring.md)).

| Component                             | Default size | Default enter | Layer   | Purpose                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`title`](#title)                     | 960×240      | rise          | base    | Big display text; **accent** markup colors words with the accent color.                                                               |
| [`label`](#label)                     | 640×60       | fade          | base    | Small uppercase monospace label.                                                                                                      |
| [`code`](#code)                       | 960×520      | rise          | base    | Code card with token colors that types itself.                                                                                        |
| [`node`](#node)                       | 300×170      | pop           | base    | Box with a title and a sub-status; status changes its color.                                                                          |
| [`arrow`](#arrow)                     | 200×40       | draw          | overlay | Straight, elbow or curved arrow with an optional label and moving packets.                                                            |
| [`chip`](#chip)                       | 340×84       | pop           | base    | Pill/tag, optionally struck through.                                                                                                  |
| [`stamp`](#stamp)                     | 680×260      | stamp         | overlay | Rotated bordered word that slams in (×2, DEADLOCK).                                                                                   |
| [`table`](#table)                     | 960×440      | pop           | base    | Header + rows with animated row inserts and highlights.                                                                               |
| [`lanes`](#lanes)                     | 960×760      | pop           | base    | Parallel columns of timed steps (race conditions).                                                                                    |
| [`checklist`](#checklist)             | 880×460      | pop           | base    | Items with check boxes appearing in sequence.                                                                                         |
| [`counter`](#counter)                 | 820×320      | pop           | base    | Big number counting between keyframe values.                                                                                          |
| [`meter`](#meter)                     | 880×180      | pop           | base    | Horizontal bar (or a half-circle gauge with `style: gauge`) with an optional threshold marker.                                        |
| [`timeline`](#timeline)               | 960×260      | pop           | base    | Axis with markers at relative positions (backoff, TTL).                                                                               |
| [`grid`](#grid)                       | 640×640      | pop           | base    | N×M tiles with per-tile states (thread pool, shards, services).                                                                       |
| [`bucket`](#bucket)                   | 440×560      | pop           | base    | Token bucket whose tokens are consumed and refilled over time.                                                                        |
| [`phone`](#phone)                     | 440×880      | pop           | base    | Phone mock with a checkout screen, button taps and notifications.                                                                     |
| [`quote`](#quote)                     | 940×460      | rise          | base    | Quote card with author; the quote types itself.                                                                                       |
| [`particles`](#particles)             | 1080×1000    | none          | overlay | Seeded particle bursts, herds, streams, dust or confetti.                                                                             |
| [`trap`](#trap)                       | 1080×1000    | glitch        | overlay | The series "THE TRAP" interstitial with warning tapes.                                                                                |
| [`cta`](#cta)                         | 960×560      | rise          | base    | "Next episode" title plus a comment box typing a keyword.                                                                             |
| [`icon`](#icon)                       | 160×160      | pop           | base    | Inline SVG icon from the bundled set, or an SVG from assets/.                                                                         |
| [`bar-chart`](#bar-chart)             | 960×560      | fade          | base    | Vertical or horizontal bars that grow in on enter; keyframable values and a focus bar.                                                |
| [`line-chart`](#line-chart)           | 960×560      | fade          | base    | One or more series that draw themselves, with points, axis labels and a legend.                                                       |
| [`donut-chart`](#donut-chart)         | 960×520      | fade          | base    | Donut whose segments sweep in, with a center value and a legend.                                                                      |
| [`stat-card`](#stat-card)             | 420×260      | rise          | base    | KPI card: a value counting up, a label and an up/down delta.                                                                          |
| [`progress-ring`](#progress-ring)     | 360×360      | pop           | base    | Circular percentage that fills to its value (keyframable).                                                                            |
| [`comparison`](#comparison)           | 960×560      | rise          | base    | A vs B columns with rows of attributes (check/cross or values) and a winner.                                                          |
| [`before-after`](#before-after)       | 960×520      | rise          | base    | Two panels (text or an assets/ image) revealed by an animated wipe divider.                                                           |
| [`ranking`](#ranking)                 | 960×560      | fade          | base    | Ordered horizontal bars with rank numbers that grow in sequence.                                                                      |
| [`steps`](#steps)                     | 760×620      | fade          | base    | Numbered steps appearing one by one, vertical or horizontal.                                                                          |
| [`flow`](#flow)                       | 960×300      | fade          | base    | Horizontal pipeline of stages with connectors and a moving token.                                                                     |
| [`org-chart`](#org-chart)             | 960×560      | fade          | base    | Tree of person/role boxes (nested or parent ids) with automatic layout.                                                               |
| [`tree`](#tree)                       | 960×560      | fade          | base    | Generic hierarchy with automatic layout; branches draw in level by level.                                                             |
| [`cycle`](#cycle)                     | 760×760      | fade          | base    | Stages around a circle with arrows; the active stage is highlighted over time.                                                        |
| [`funnel`](#funnel)                   | 760×620      | fade          | base    | Stages narrowing from top to bottom, with values and optional conversion rates.                                                       |
| [`pyramid`](#pyramid)                 | 760×620      | fade          | base    | Stacked levels from a narrow top to a wide base, labelled at the side.                                                                |
| [`matrix-2x2`](#matrix-2x2)           | 760×760      | fade          | base    | 2×2 quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) with axis labels and placed items.                                     |
| [`map`](#map)                         | 960×600      | fade          | base    | World or regional outline map (Natural Earth, public domain): highlighted countries, labelled pins and routes that draw between them. |

| [`container-stack`](#container-stack) | 860×560      | fade          | base    | Shipping containers with their codes, stacked bottom-up like a crane loads them.                                                      |
| [`calendar`](#calendar)               | 760×700      | fade          | base    | Month view (English or Arabic names) whose highlighted days appear over time.                                                         |
| [`clock`](#clock)                     | 420×420      | pop           | base    | Analog or digital clock that ticks between keyframed times, or a countdown (`mode: countdown`).                                       |

| [`chat`](#chat)                       | 760×760      | fade          | base    | Message bubbles (left/right, LTR or RTL) that appear in order, with a typing indicator.                                               |
| [`notification`](#notification)       | 760×520      | fade          | base    | Stack of notification toasts sliding in one after another (newest on top).                                                            |

| [`qr-code`](#qr-code)                 | 420×500      | fade          | base    | Scannable QR code (byte mode, ECC L or M, versions 1–10) encoded in the runtime.                                                      |
| [`rating`](#rating)                   | 640×200      | pop           | base    | Stars from 0 to max with halves, filling in turn. For illustrative scores only, never as real customer reviews.                       |
| [`vitals`](#vitals)                   | 860×360      | fade          | base    | Heart-rate monitor: an ECG trace sweeping across with a live BPM counter (keyframable).                                               |

## title

Big display text; **accent** markup colors words with the accent color.

| Prop     | Type                                      | Default    | Required |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------- |
| `text`   | string                                    |            | yes      |
| `size`   | number                                    |            |          |
| `align`  | `left` \| `center` \| `right`             | `"center"` |          |
| `color`  | string                                    | `"ink"`    |          |
| `accent` | string                                    | `"lime"`   |          |
| `font`   | `auto` \| `display` \| `arabic` \| `mono` | `"auto"`   |          |
| `weight` | integer                                   | `800`      |          |
| `sub`    | string                                    |            |          |

## progress-ring

| Prop        | Type                 | Default  | Required |
| ----------- | -------------------- | -------- | -------- |
| `value`     | number               |          | yes      |
| `max`       | number               | `100`    |          |

<!-- file: docs/guide/adr.md -->

# Architecture decision records

Each decision record (ADR) documents one significant design decision: its context, the decision and its
consequences. The [architecture guide](../architecture.md) explains how the decisions fit together in
the code.

| ADR                                                     | Decision                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| [001](../adr/001-dom-svg-rendering-surface.md)          | DOM/SVG in headless Chromium as the rendering surface  |
| [002](../adr/002-yaml-single-source-of-truth.md)        | YAML is the only authoring format                      |
| [003](../adr/003-pure-render-determinism.md)            | Pure `render(t)` and determinism rules                 |
| [004](../adr/004-human-marked-cues.md)                  | Human-marked cues (superseded in part by ADR-013)      |
| [005](../adr/005-parallel-frame-range-workers.md)       | Parallel frame-range workers and segment concatenation |
| [006](../adr/006-master-and-share-outputs.md)           | Two outputs: master and size-targeted share file       |
| [007](../adr/007-caption-bidi-strategy.md)              | Caption bidi strategy                                  |
| [008](../adr/008-procedural-sfx.md)                     | Procedural sound effects instead of sample libraries   |
| [009](../adr/009-system-ffmpeg.md)                      | System FFmpeg instead of a bundled binary              |
| [010](../adr/010-monorepo-package-boundaries.md)        | Monorepo with pnpm workspaces and package boundaries   |
| [011](../adr/011-static-grain-by-default.md)            | Static film grain by default                           |
| [012](../adr/012-project-dashboard.md)                  | A project dashboard with write actions                 |
| [013](../adr/013-assisted-cue-alignment.md)             | Assisted cue alignment                                 |
| [014](../adr/014-one-tool-registry-three-transports.md) | One tool registry, three transports                    |
| [015](../adr/015-local-server-security.md)              | Local server security for AI endpoints                 |
| [016](../adr/016-vertical-only-formats.md)              | 9:16 is the only format for 1.0                        |

For a significant design change, add a new record in `docs/adr/` (see [Contributing](contributing.md)).

<!-- file: docs/guide/ai.md -->

# AI integration

ReelForge works on its own: you write the script, design scenes in the editor and render. If you use an
AI assistant, it can do the heavy lifting: write the script, build every scene, look at rendered frames
and fix problems. You stay in control. You record your own voice, check the cues by ear and approve the
result in the editor.

The render engine contains no AI: it draws every frame deterministically from `episode.yaml`. Two optional
helpers run on your computer:

- **Speech alignment** (`align_cues`, `reelforge align`) marks every line and word from `voice.wav`.
  It works from pause detection alone; `reelforge align --setup` downloads the optional speech models
  (Whisper and Silero VAD) once, and after that alignment runs offline.
- **Scene suggestions** (`suggest_scene`, `suggest_scenes`) use a built-in keyword dictionary, or a
  language model you configure (see [Local and cloud models](#models)).

## Three ways in

All three serve the same tools from one registry, so names, arguments and results are identical
(ADR-014). The [MCP tools reference](../reference/mcp-tools.md) lists every tool.

| Transport           | Start it                             | Endpoint                       | Use it for                                      |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| MCP over stdio      | your client runs `reelforge mcp`     | standard input/output          | Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI |
| MCP Streamable HTTP | `reelforge studio` (keep it running) | `http://127.0.0.1:4310/mcp`    | clients that prefer a URL, several clients      |
| REST and OpenAPI    | `reelforge studio`                   | `http://127.0.0.1:4310/api/v1` | agent frameworks with function calling          |

```bash
./reelforge mcp          # macOS / Linux
reelforge.cmd mcp        # Windows
```

You don't run the stdio server yourself: your client starts it when needed. It runs on your computer and
never sends your files anywhere; the AI service only sees what your client sends it.

The REST API answers `GET /api/v1/tools` (add `?format=openai` for OpenAI function definitions),
`POST /api/v1/tools/<name>` with the arguments as JSON, and `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` for GPT Actions and
other OpenAPI importers. The dashboard also serves `/.well-known/mcp.json` (a server card) and
`/llms.txt` / `/llms-full.txt` (the documentation in one file).

## Client setup

The project folder already contains configuration for Claude Code (`.mcp.json`), Cursor
(`.cursor/mcp.json`), VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`) and Gemini CLI (`.gemini/settings.json`). Open the folder
in the client and approve the `reelforge` server. For example, with Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add reelforge -- node packages/cli/bin/reelforge.js mcp
```

Try: _"Make a 40-second English episode about database indexes, preview it and fix any issues."_

Every other client (Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Codex CLI, Zed, Continue, LM Studio and any OpenAI-compatible
framework), in stdio and HTTP variants, is in [AI client setup](../reference/ai-clients.md). The dashboard's
**Connect AI** page (`/connect`) shows the same snippets with your real paths and a connection test.

## Toolsets

Small context windows work better with fewer tools. Ask for one or more toolsets:

```bash
reelforge mcp --toolsets basic,design
```

Over HTTP use `/mcp?toolsets=basic` (also on `/api/v1/tools` and `/api/v1/openapi.json`).

| Toolset  | Contains                                                                         |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `basic`  | read, create (from a script or a template), add scenes, validate, preview, cues  |
| `design` | structured edits, full YAML, component schemas, blueprints and scene suggestions |
| `render` | render, status, cancel, open the editor, environment check                       |
| `all`    | every tool (the default)                                                         |

## Tool tiers

Pick the tools that match the model's strength. Every write tool returns the validation summary, one fix
hint per problem (`fixes`) and the recommended next step (`next`), so any model can correct itself in a loop.

| Tier | For           | Tools                                                        | The model writes                      |
| ---- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| 1    | small models  | `list_templates` → `create_from_template`, `suggest_scenes`  | a flat object of slot values; no YAML |
| 2    | medium models | `create_episode`, `list_blueprints` → `add_scene`            | the script and a few fields per scene |
| 3    | strong models | `edit_episode`, `write_episode_yaml`, `get_component_schema` | any element, prop, time and animation |

Shared tools for every tier: `get_episode`, `validate_episode`, `preview_frames` (images for vision models
plus a text layout description for text-only models), `draft_cues`, `align_cues`, `set_cues`,
`render_episode`, `get_render_status`, `cancel_render`, `open_editor`, `doctor` and `get_guide`.

## Skills and instruction files

Task guides live in `skills/` in the Agent Skills format (one folder per skill with `SKILL.md` and
`references/`). Clients that support skills load them directly; others call `get_guide` (`topic`, and
`detail: true` for the full guide). `.claude-plugin/` packages the skills with the MCP server as a Claude
Code plugin.

| Skill                            | Covers                                                     |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `reelforge-make-video`           | the end-to-end workflow and which tool tier to use         |
| `reelforge-script-writing`       | hooks, one idea per line, words per second, Arabic terms   |
| `reelforge-scene-design`         | layout, safe zones, component choice, motion rules         |
| `reelforge-timing`               | cues, word anchors, automatic alignment                    |
| `reelforge-industry-playbooks`   | audience, tone, templates and compliance per industry      |
| `reelforge-brand-and-themes`     | themes from brand colors and fonts, contrast               |
| `reelforge-review-and-render`    | the validation loop, visual QA, render options, publishing |
| `reelforge-contribute-component` | adding a component correctly                               |

| Instruction file                  | Read by                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AGENTS.md`                       | Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Zed, Aider, Jules and most agents |
| `CLAUDE.md`                       | Claude Code (imports AGENTS.md)                                     |
| `GEMINI.md`                       | Gemini CLI (imports AGENTS.md)                                      |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | GitHub Copilot                                                      |
| `.cursor/rules/reelforge.mdc`     | Cursor                                                              |
| `.windsurf/rules/reelforge.md`    | Windsurf                                                            |
| `llms.txt`                        | Assistants that look for an llms.txt index                          |

Edit them to add your house style, for example your series' colors, tone of voice or standard ending.

## Local and cloud models {#models}

ReelForge's own scene suggestions can use a language model. Nothing is configured by default; without a
model, suggestions come from the keyword dictionary. Set environment variables, or write `llm.json` in the
ReelForge config folder (`%APPDATA%\reelforge`, `~/Library/Application Support/reelforge` or
`~/.config/reelforge`) with the same keys (`provider`, `baseUrl`, `model`, `apiKey`).

| Variable                 | Meaning                                                              |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `REELFORGE_LLM_PROVIDER` | `openai` (any OpenAI-compatible server), `anthropic` or `ollama`     |
| `REELFORGE_LLM_BASE_URL` | Server URL; the provider is guessed from it when not set             |
| `REELFORGE_LLM_MODEL`    | Model name                                                           |
| `REELFORGE_LLM_API_KEY`  | API key for cloud services (stored only in your environment or file) |

```bash
# Local model through Ollama (default address 127.0.0.1:11434)
REELFORGE_LLM_PROVIDER=ollama REELFORGE_LLM_MODEL=qwen2.5:1.5b reelforge studio

# LM Studio, llama.cpp server, vLLM or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
REELFORGE_LLM_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 REELFORGE_LLM_MODEL=my-model reelforge studio

# A cloud API
REELFORGE_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic REELFORGE_LLM_API_KEY=... reelforge studio
```

On Windows PowerShell set variables with `$env:REELFORGE_LLM_MODEL = "qwen2.5:1.5b"` before the command.
Answers are constrained to the component schemas (JSON Schema output where the server supports it, a
grammar on Ollama, otherwise a validate-and-repair loop). The dashboard shows which model is in use.

## Evaluating models

`scripts/eval-agents.mjs` runs one authoring task per industry against a model through the real tool
registry and scores each produced episode: created, valid, no overlaps, inside the safe zones, right
language, every line covered (and, with `--render`, renders).

```bash
pnpm build
node scripts/eval-agents.mjs --mock                                   # scripted model, offline (CI)
node scripts/eval-agents.mjs --base-url http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 --model qwen2.5:7b
node scripts/eval-agents.mjs --base-url https://api.example.com/v1 --model my-model --api-key "$KEY" \
  --toolsets basic --tasks healthcare,finance --out results.md
```

The endpoint must speak OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions with tool calling. Publish results with this
table (the script writes it with `--out`):

| Model | Toolsets | Industry | Lang | Score | Calls | Tool errors | Time (s) |
| ----- | -------- | -------- | ---- | ----- | ----- | ----------- | -------- |
|       | basic    | …        | en   | %     |       |             |          |
|       | basic    | **all**  |      | **%** |       |             |          |

## Security {#security}

- The dashboard and editor bind to `127.0.0.1`. Every request must carry a loopback `Host` (or a name in
  `REELFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS`), which blocks DNS rebinding; no CORS headers are sent and writes are JSON-only.
- `reelforge studio --host <address>` (or `REELFORGE_HOST`) binds elsewhere. Then `/mcp` and `/api/v1`
  require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and other computers can reach only the AI endpoints, never the
  dashboard UI. `REELFORGE_REQUIRE_TOKEN=1` requires the token on loopback too.
- The token is created on first use and stored in the config folder (`token`, readable only by you where
  the system supports it). The Connect AI page shows it only to a browser on the same computer.
- Plain HTTP carries the token in clear text: on an untrusted network, put the dashboard behind a TLS proxy.
- Tools only read and write inside the project folder; renders are served only from `out/`.

ADR-015 records the full design.

## Tips

- **Ask the assistant to look.** Say _"preview the frames and fix anything that looks off"_. The
  assistant receives the frames as images.
- **Keep the voice human.** ReelForge never generates voices. Record yourself, let `align_cues`
  mark the lines and words, then listen through once in the editor's **Cues** mode and fix any line
  by ear.
- **Review in the editor.** Ask for `open_editor` to get a link. Everything the assistant wrote is
  editable visually, and every change can be undone.
- **Large changes:** the assistant can rewrite the whole `episode.yaml`. The file is checked before
  it is saved, and invalid YAML is refused.

<!-- file: docs/guide/command-line.md -->

# Command line

On Windows use `reelforge.cmd`; on macOS/Linux `./reelforge` (or add the folder to your PATH). From a source
checkout, `pnpm reelforge` works everywhere. Every command and option is listed in the
[CLI reference](../reference/cli.md), generated from the command definition itself.

![CLI help](../screenshots/19-cli-help.png)

## Main commands

| Command                                                                        | Description                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `reelforge studio [--port <n>] [--host <address>] [--no-open]`                 | Open the project dashboard (default `http://127.0.0.1:4310`)                                   |
| `reelforge new <id> [--series <name>] [--episode <n>] [--lang en\|ar]`         | Create `episodes/<id>/episode.yaml` from the blank starter                                     |
| `reelforge new <id> --pack <pack> [--template <t>] [--lang ar] [--slot k=v …]` | Create it from an industry template, with draft cues (see [Templates](templates-and-packs.md)) |
| `reelforge packs [--lang en\|ar]`                                              | List the industry packs, their templates and slots (`--json` for the full slot definitions)    |
| `reelforge edit <id>`                                                          | Open the visual editor                                                                         |
| `reelforge cue <id> [--draft]`                                                 | Open the editor in Cues mode (`--draft` writes estimated cues instead)                         |
| `reelforge align <id> [--engine dsp\|whisper] [--force] [--dry-run]`           | Cues for every line and word from the recording (see [Timing](timing.md))                      |
| `reelforge align --setup [--model tiny\|base\|small]` / `--status`             | Install / show the optional speech models (one time, ~180 MB)                                  |
| `reelforge dev <id>`                                                           | Open the editor in Review mode                                                                 |
| `reelforge mcp [--toolsets basic,design,render]`                               | Run the MCP server for AI assistants (see [AI integration](ai.md))                             |
| `reelforge validate <id> [--strict] [--no-measure]`                            | Check everything; exit code 1 on errors (or warnings with `--strict`)                          |
| `reelforge render <id> [options]` / `--all`                                    | Render (see [Rendering and publishing](rendering.md))                                          |
| `reelforge snap <id> <times…> [--every 5] [--cover]`                           | PNG frames + contact sheet; times may be `12.5`, `l7`, `"l7:'word'"`                           |
| `reelforge doctor [--fix]`                                                     | Check the environment; `--fix` downloads Chromium                                              |
| `reelforge theme new <name> --accent <#hex> [--mode light\|dark] [--font <f>]` | Generate a full theme (contrast-checked) from an accent color                                  |
| `reelforge schema [--out <file>]`                                              | Write the JSON Schema for editor autocompletion                                                |

Global options: `--json` (machine-readable output, progress events while rendering), `--verbose`,
`--root <folder>` (project folder; default: the current folder).

![validate](../screenshots/21-cli-validate.png)

`reelforge align` options: `--engine auto|dsp|whisper` (auto: Whisper when installed, else pause
detection), `--model tiny|base|small`, `--no-vad`, `--no-words` (line cues only), `--force` (replace cues
you marked by hand), `--dry-run` (print, don't write). `reelforge render --denoise` / `--no-denoise`
overrides `audio.denoise`.

## Environment variables

| Variable                                | Meaning                                                           |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `REELFORGE_ROOT`                        | Project folder                                                    |
| `REELFORGE_PRESET`                      | Default preset                                                    |
| `REELFORGE_WORKERS`                     | Render processes                                                  |
| `REELFORGE_SHARE_SIZE`                  | Share size in MB                                                  |
| `REELFORGE_JPEG_QUALITY`                | Frame capture quality (default 95)                                |
| `REELFORGE_PORT`                        | Dashboard / studio port                                           |
| `REELFORGE_HOST`                        | Dashboard bind address (default 127.0.0.1)                        |
| `REELFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS`               | Extra Host names the dashboard accepts (comma separated)          |
| `REELFORGE_REQUIRE_TOKEN`               | `1` requires the bearer token on `/mcp` and `/api/v1` everywhere  |
| `REELFORGE_NO_OPEN`                     | Do not open the browser automatically                             |
| `REELFORGE_FFMPEG`, `REELFORGE_FFPROBE` | Paths to ffmpeg / ffprobe                                         |
| `REELFORGE_CHROMIUM`                    | Path to a Chromium executable                                     |
| `REELFORGE_CACHE`                       | Folder for the optional speech models                             |
| `REELFORGE_CONFIG_DIR`                  | Config folder (`llm.json`, the server token)                      |
| `REELFORGE_LLM_*`                       | Language model for scene suggestions (see [models](ai.md#models)) |
| `NO_COLOR`                              | Disable colors                                                    |

<!-- file: docs/guide/contributing.md -->

# Contributing

Contributions are welcome under the Apache License 2.0 (documentation and examples under CC BY 4.0).
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) in the repository covers the development setup on Windows, macOS
and Linux, commit conventions and the quality gate every pull request must pass:

```bash
pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test:unit && pnpm test:browser
```

This page describes the four most common contributions.

## Add a component

1. Add its prop schema and defaults in `packages/core/src/components/`. Props are strict Zod objects; give
   every prop a sensible default so the editor can insert the component with no input.
2. Add its runtime in `packages/runtime/src/components/`. It draws DOM/SVG for any time `t` and must stay
   pure: no `Date.now()`, no unseeded randomness, no timers. Support right-to-left layout.
3. Add a scene that shows it to the gallery in `fixtures/golden/components/episode.yaml`.
4. Refresh the golden frames and review every changed image:
   `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 pnpm test:browser` (PowerShell:
   `$env:UPDATE_GOLDEN=1; pnpm test:browser; Remove-Item Env:UPDATE_GOLDEN`).
5. Regenerate the documentation with `pnpm docs:gen`. The [components reference](../reference/components.md)
   picks up the schema and the new gallery frame.

The `reelforge-contribute-component` skill has a detailed checklist.

## Add a theme

Copy `themes/default.theme.yaml` to `themes/<name>.theme.yaml` and change the tokens, or generate one with
`pnpm reelforge theme new <name> --accent "#hex"`. Use only bundled fonts and keep the contrast rules in
[Themes and branding](themes.md): the theme test checks WCAG AA for every bundled theme. Check it with an
example episode (`meta.theme: <name>`) and `reelforge snap`. Themes contain no code.

## Add an industry pack

A pack lives in `packs/<id>/`:

```text
packs/<id>/
  pack.yaml                     manifest: names, description, theme, blueprints, templates and slots
  templates/<template>.en.yaml  an episode with {{slot}} placeholders (one file per language)
  templates/<template>.ar.yaml
  examples/<name>-en/           a complete example episode (generated)
  examples/<name>-ar/
```

1. Open an [industry pack request](https://github.com/TerminalDZ/vidcreat/issues/new?template=industry_pack_request.yml)
   first so the scope can be agreed.
2. Write `pack.yaml`; it is validated by the pack schema in `packages/core/src/packs.ts` when loaded. Use
   fictional organization names only, and keep slot limits tight enough that text fits its box.
3. Write each template in English and Arabic. Every element should enter on a word of the script.
4. Add the example to `scripts/gen-pack-examples.mjs` and run it; then validate the examples and render them
   with `--silent`.
5. Add a playbook in `skills/reelforge-industry-playbooks/references/<id>.md` (audience, tone, typical
   episodes, compliance), and run `pnpm docs:gen` to update the [pack catalog](../reference/packs.md).

## Add a skill

Skills live in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in the Agent Skills format: YAML front matter with a `name` and a
one-sentence `description` of when to use the skill, followed by concise Markdown instructions; longer
material goes in `references/`. Keep each skill focused on one task, refer only to commands and files that
exist, and test it by following the instructions yourself on a fresh episode. `pnpm check:skills` (part of
`pnpm lint`) checks the format, and `get_guide` serves the new skill automatically.

## Documentation

The site and the offline documentation are built from the same Markdown in `docs/`:

| Command           | What it does                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm docs:gen`   | Regenerates the reference pages, component frames, `docs/components.md`, `llms-full.txt`                         |
| `pnpm docs:dev`   | Serves the site locally with live reload                                                                         |
| `pnpm docs:site`  | Builds the public site (base `/vidcreat/`) into `docs/.site` (fails on dead links)                               |
| `pnpm docs:local` | Builds the same site with base `/docs/` into `documentation/site`, which the dashboard serves at `/docs/`        |
| `pnpm docs:build` | Runs `docs:gen`, the single-file `documentation/index.html` (English and Arabic) and `docs:local`; commit result |

English pages live in `docs/guide/` and `docs/reference/`; their Arabic versions mirror them under
`docs/ar/`. Never edit generated pages by hand: CI runs `node scripts/check-docs-fresh.mjs` and fails when
they are out of date. In Arabic pages, keep technical terms, commands and YAML keys in English inside
backticks, and avoid starting a paragraph with a Latin word.

## Decision records

For a significant design change, add an ADR in `docs/adr/` (next number, context, decision, consequences).

---

<!-- file: docs/guide/dashboard.md -->

# The dashboard

`reelforge studio` (or `start.bat` / `start.sh`) opens the dashboard at `http://127.0.0.1:4310`. It lists
**your episodes** (the `episodes/` folder) and the **examples**.

![Dashboard](../screenshots/00-dashboard.jpg)

Each card shows a live thumbnail, the series, preset, number of lines and scenes, the duration, and status
chips:

| Chip                                    | Meaning                                                 |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `voice 1:15` / `no voice`               | Whether a recording is present, and its length          |
| `cues 24/24` / `draft cues` / `no cues` | How many sentences are marked; draft cues are estimates |
| `valid` / `2 warnings` / `1 error`      | Result of the static checks (hover an error to read it) |

| Button           | What it does                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Upload voice** | Choose a recording; it is converted to `voice.wav` (48 kHz)                                                        |
| **Open editor**  | Opens the visual editor for this episode in a new tab (see [The editor](editor.md))                                |
| **Mark cues**    | Opens the editor in Cues mode, ready to mark when each sentence starts                                             |
| **Auto cues**    | Aligns every line and word to the recording (see [Timing, cues and alignment](timing.md))                          |
| **Validate**     | Runs every check, including the headless text-overflow and caption checks                                          |
| **Render**       | Choose the platform preset, share size, SFX and speed; progress, FPS and ETA appear live; **Cancel** stops cleanly |
| **Folder**       | Opens the episode folder in your file manager                                                                      |
| **Draft cues**   | (only without cues) estimates timing from the text                                                                 |

To start from an industry template, click **+ New episode** and choose **Start from template**: pick a pack
and a template, fill in the fields and the language, and the episode opens in the editor (see
[Templates and packs](templates-and-packs.md)).

![Validation results](../screenshots/23-dashboard-validate.jpg)

![Render options](../screenshots/24-dashboard-render-options.jpg)

![Live render progress](../screenshots/25-dashboard-render-progress.jpg)

Finished outputs appear as links on the card: videos open in a player with a **Download** button.

![Built-in player](../screenshots/26-dashboard-player.jpg)

The **Gallery** page (`/gallery`) shows what you can build with. **Components** lists all 62 components by
category with a search box and a preview frame from the component gallery; click one for its props and a YAML
snippet to copy. **Themes** previews every built-in and project theme from its colors and fonts, with its light
or dark mode and a WCAG contrast check. **Packs** lists the industry packs in English or Arabic; **Use this
template** opens the new-episode dialog with that template selected.

The **Connect AI** page (`/connect`) has copy-paste setup for AI clients; see [AI integration](ai.md).

The **Documentation** button opens this documentation at `/docs/`, served from your ReelForge folder, so it
works offline. It has the same pages as the online site, in English and Arabic (switch with the language
menu), with search.

Only one render runs at a time. The dashboard listens on `127.0.0.1` by default, so other computers cannot
reach it. `--host` binds it elsewhere and then requires a bearer token for the AI endpoints (see
[security](ai.md#security)).

---

<!-- file: docs/guide/editor.md -->

# The editor

The editor is where you design an episode. It works like a design tool on top of a video
timeline, but it is made for one job. You place animated components on the real
1080×1920 frame and time them to the words you speak.

Open it from the dashboard with **Open editor**, or run `reelforge edit <id>`. `reelforge cue <id>` opens
it in Cues mode and `reelforge dev <id>` in Review mode.

![The editor](../screenshots/01-editor-overview.jpg)

| Area            | What it holds                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Top bar**     | Modes (Edit · Cues · Review), undo/redo, transport and speed, status, checks, search, **Render** |
| **Left panel**  | **Layers** (scenes → elements), **Insert** (every component) and **Script** (your lines)         |
| **Canvas**      | The real frame, rendered by the same engine as the final video, synced to your voice             |
| **Right panel** | The **Inspector** for whatever is selected (or the episode settings when nothing is)             |
| **Timeline**    | Chapters, scenes, script lines, one track per layer, and your voice waveform with sound effects  |

Every change is written to `episode.yaml` immediately, and your comments and formatting are kept.
Every change can also be undone (**⌘Z** / **Ctrl+Z**), including cue changes. You can keep
`episode.yaml` open in a text editor at the same time. Edits made there appear in the editor as
soon as you save.

## Canvas

- **Click** an element to select it. **Alt+click** selects the one underneath. Hover shows an
  outline.
- **Drag** to move. Smart guides snap to the frame center, the scene area and other elements. Hold
  **Shift** to move in a straight line, or **Alt** to turn snapping off.
- **Drag a handle** to resize. Hold **Shift** to keep the proportions, or **Alt** to resize from the
  center.
- Use the **arrow keys** to nudge 1 px (**Shift**: 10 px).
- **Double-click** a title, label, chip, stamp, quote, node or ending card to **edit its text in
  place**. Press **Enter** to save or **Esc** to cancel.
- **Drag a component** from **Insert** onto the canvas to add it there.
- **Zoom** with **⌘/Ctrl + wheel**, **Shift+1** (fit), **Shift+2** (selection) or **Shift+0**
  (100%). **Pan** with the wheel, by holding **Space**, or with the **H** tool.
- The floating toolbar toggles the **safe zones** (**Z**, where TikTok/Reels/Shorts draw their
  buttons), **stage and caption guides** (**B**) and **element outlines** (**E**).

![Moving with smart guides](../screenshots/02-editor-drag-guides.jpg)

## Layers, Insert and Script

**Layers** lists every scene and its elements. The top of each list is drawn on top. Click to select
(the playhead jumps to a moment when the element is visible), **drag** to reorder, and
**double-click** to rename. Renaming also updates any arrows that point at the element. A green dot
marks what is on screen at the playhead.

**Insert** shows all 62 components in groups: Text, Diagrams, Data, Charts, Process & structure, Places &
movement, Time, People & messaging, Media & text, Health & data, Code & devices, Effects & endings.
**Click** one to add it to the current scene at the playhead, or drag it onto the canvas. New
elements start with sensible content that you can change at once.

![Insert panel](../screenshots/04-editor-insert.jpg)

**Script** is your text, one spoken sentence per line. Edit a line in place. Use the line's buttons
to add, delete or reorder lines. Arabic, English and mixed lines are all supported, and the
direction is detected automatically.

## Inspector

The inspector edits **every property** of the selection:

- **Position & size** (X, Y, W, H), alignment buttons, layer and stacking order.
- **Animation & timing**: when it enters, the animation, its ease and duration, and an optional
  exit. **Preview animation** plays just that moment once; choosing a new animation or ease
  previews it automatically. The
  **target** button sets a time from the playhead. It writes a word-anchored time such as
  `l3:'bucket'` whenever the playhead is on a word, so the element stays on that word even after
  you re-record.
- **Properties**: every option of the component, generated from its schema. That covers text
  fields, numbers (drag the dotted handle to scrub), on/off switches, menus, colors
  (theme swatches or any color), times, and lists you can add to, reorder and remove from.
- **Effects** (shake, flash, glitch, pulse, bump) and **States** (prop changes at a time, e.g. a
  node turning red).
- **Sound**: automatic sound effects on or off.
- **YAML (advanced)**: the exact YAML of the element. Anything the format supports can be edited
  here.

With a **scene** selected, the inspector edits its start and end, transition, camera move (with **Preview transition**), area (stage or full
frame), background glow and auto-layout. With a **script line** selected, it edits the text,
caption, line breaks and cue, and lists every word (click one to jump to it). With **nothing**
selected, it edits the episode: title, series, platform, theme, language, publishing texts, audio
and chapters.

![Script line in the inspector](../screenshots/11-editor-script.jpg)

## Timeline

![Retiming a clip on the timeline](../screenshots/03-editor-timeline.jpg)

- **Click or drag the ruler** to move the playhead. Chapters are shown on the ruler.
- **Scenes**: drag a scene's start to move it.
- **Script**: each line is a clip. Drag it to change its cue. Its word marks move with it.
- **Layer tracks**: each element is a clip from when it enters to when it leaves.
  - Drag the **body** to retime it.
  - Drag the **left edge** to change when it enters.
  - Drag the **right edge** to set when it leaves. Dragging it to the end of the scene removes the
    exit.
  - Diamonds mark effects (orange) and state changes (blue).
- Clips snap to **words**, line starts, scenes and the playhead. The badge shows the time
  expression that will be saved. Hold **Alt** to drag freely, or press **S** to turn snapping off.
- **I** and **O** set the selected element's in and out points at the playhead.
- **Zoom** with **= / −**, the slider or **⌘/Ctrl + wheel**. **\\** fits the whole episode.

## Search everything: ⌘K / Ctrl+K

The command palette finds every command, component, scene, element and script line. Type a few
letters and press **Enter**. Try `insert counter`, `go to scene trap` or `safe zones`.

![Command palette](../screenshots/05-editor-palette.jpg)

Right-click the canvas, a layer or a clip for the most common actions. Press **?** to see every
shortcut.

![Keyboard shortcuts](../screenshots/06-editor-shortcuts.jpg)

## Review mode

**Review** (**Alt+3**, or click the checks pill in the top bar) lists every issue found by the
checks: schema, timing, overlaps, safe zones, text overflow measured in the real browser, and
caption length. Each issue has a fix hint. Click an issue to jump to its time and select the
element.

![Review mode](../screenshots/09-editor-review.jpg)

If `episode.yaml` has a syntax error (for example after editing it by hand), a banner shows the line
and the message. The editor keeps showing the last version that worked.

## Rendering from the editor

Click **Render** (**⌘/Ctrl+Enter**) and choose the platform, the share-file size, sound effects,
silent mode (when there is no recording yet) and a fast draft. You can keep editing while it
renders, and the progress shows in the top bar. When it finishes, the videos open in a player with
download links.

![Render](../screenshots/12-editor-render.jpg)

## Shortcuts at a glance

| Keys                                     | Action                                 |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| **Space** / **K**                        | Play / pause                           |
| **J** / **L**, **,** / **.**             | −1 s / +1 s, previous / next frame     |
| **Home** / **End**                       | Start / end                            |
| **1 2 3**                                | Speed 0.5× 0.75× 1×                    |
| **⌘/Ctrl+Z**, **⌘/Ctrl+Shift+Z**         | Undo, redo                             |
| **⌘/Ctrl+D**, **⌘/Ctrl+C**, **⌘/Ctrl+V** | Duplicate, copy, paste at the playhead |
| **Delete**                               | Delete the selection                   |
| **⌘/Ctrl+]**, **⌘/Ctrl+[**               | Bring forward, send backward           |
| **I** / **O**                            | Enter / exit at the playhead           |
| **A**                                    | Insert a component                     |
| **N**                                    | Add a scene at the playhead            |
| **Tab** / **Shift+Tab**                  | Next / previous element                |
| **Z**, **B**, **E**                      | Safe zones, stage guides, outlines     |
| **S**                                    | Snapping                               |
| **Alt+1 / 2 / 3**                        | Edit / Cues / Review                   |
| **⌘/Ctrl+K**                             | Command palette                        |
| **?**                                    | All shortcuts                          |
