<!-- file: docs/guide/faq.md -->

# FAQ and troubleshooting

## Setup

**The dashboard says “setup issues”.** Click the pill: each failed check shows its fix. Most often ffmpeg is
missing (Windows: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`, macOS: `brew install ffmpeg`, Linux: your package
manager). Then restart `start.bat` / `start.sh`.

**“Cannot launch Chromium”.** Run `reelforge doctor --fix`. On Linux, also run the installer again and
accept the system libraries prompt.

**“ffmpeg not found” although I installed it (Windows).** Close every terminal and `start.bat`, then
reopen: Windows only picks up the new PATH in new windows.

More setup fixes are in [Installation](installation.md#troubleshooting).

## Episodes

**A word reference fails: `Word "x" not found in line l7`.** The error shows the closest word in that
line. Words are matched without punctuation and diacritics. For a word containing an apostrophe use double
quotes: `l7:"Conway's"`. You can also use the word index: `l7.3` (4th word).

**The caption wraps over three lines (V-10).** Add `break: ["word"]` to the script line to split the
caption before that word, or lower `captions.max_chars` in the theme.

**Text overflows its box (V-9).** Shorten the text, lower `fontSize`, or enlarge `place.w/h`. Titles,
quotes and stamps shrink automatically to fit.

**An element sits under the TikTok buttons (V-7).** Press **Z** in the editor to show the safe zones, and keep
content out of the red areas. In the lower part of the stage keep `x + w ≤ 920`.

**Two elements overlap (V-8).** Give the first one an `exit` before the second enters, move one of them, or
put badges and stamps on `layer: overlay`.

**A line is “spoken too fast” (V-14).** It has more than about 3.5 words per second. Split it into two lines
or shorten it.

## Fonts, languages and formats

**Can I use my own fonts?** Themes can use any bundled family (Space Grotesk, Inter, Manrope, Playfair
Display, JetBrains Mono, Cairo, Noto Kufi Arabic, Noto Naskh Arabic, Readex Pro). Fonts are bundled so
renders never depend on the machine; other fonts are not supported yet.

**Which languages are supported?** English and Arabic captions, including Arabic sentences with English
terms.

**Can I make square or landscape videos?** Not in 1.0: ReelForge renders 9:16 vertical video only
(ADR-016). Square, portrait and landscape are on the roadmap.

## Offline use, servers and AI

**Does ReelForge need the internet?** Only during installation (dependencies, Chromium, ffmpeg) and for
the one-time download of the optional speech models. Creating, editing and rendering are fully offline.
If you use an AI assistant, the assistant itself needs its own connection and account; ReelForge's MCP
server stays local.

**Can I render on a server or in CI?** Yes: everything is available from the command line (`--json` gives
machine-readable output) and works headless on Linux.

**Does ReelForge send my files anywhere?** No. The servers bind to `127.0.0.1` by default and the render
engine blocks network access. An AI client only sees what it reads through the tools.

## Rights and files

**Can I sell the videos I make?** Yes. The videos are yours, including for clients and monetized channels.
See [License](license.md).

**Where are my files?** Each episode is a folder in `episodes/` containing `episode.yaml`, `voice.wav`,
`cues.json`, `assets/` and `out/`. Back it up like any other folder (Git works well).

## Getting help

Ask in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/TerminalDZ/vidcreat/discussions) or open an
[issue](https://github.com/TerminalDZ/vidcreat/issues). Include your operating system, the output of
`reelforge doctor --json` and the command you ran with `--verbose`.

---

<!-- file: docs/guide/installation.md -->

# Installation

Clone the repository (`git clone https://github.com/TerminalDZ/vidcreat.git`) or unpack a release
archive anywhere you like (for example `Documents/ReelForge`). Avoid folders synced by OneDrive
or iCloud for faster renders.

## Windows 10 / 11

1. Install **Node.js 22 LTS** from <https://nodejs.org> (keep the default options). If it is missing, the
   installer can install it for you with `winget`.
2. Double-click **`install.bat`**. It will:
   - check Node.js,
   - offer to install **ffmpeg** with `winget` (answer **Y**),
   - install ReelForge's dependencies,
   - download the pinned Chromium browser used for rendering,
   - run a full environment check.
3. Double-click **`start.bat`** to open the dashboard.

> If Windows SmartScreen warns about the script, choose **More info → Run anyway**. If ffmpeg was just
> installed, close and reopen `start.bat` so Windows picks up the new PATH.

## macOS

1. Install **Node.js 22 LTS** from <https://nodejs.org> and **Homebrew** from <https://brew.sh>.
2. Open **Terminal** in the ReelForge folder (Finder → right-click the folder → _New Terminal at Folder_) and run:

   ```bash
   ./install.sh
   ```

   Answer **Y** when it offers `brew install ffmpeg`.

3. Double-click **`ReelForge.command`** (or run `./start.sh`) to open the dashboard.

## Linux

```bash
./install.sh          # add --yes to accept every prompt
./start.sh            # opens the dashboard
```

The installer uses your package manager (`apt`, `dnf`, `pacman` or `zypper`) for ffmpeg and can install
Chromium's system libraries (it asks for `sudo`).

## From source (developers)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/TerminalDZ/vidcreat.git && cd vidcreat
corepack enable && pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm reelforge doctor --fix
```

The [contributing guide](contributing.md) covers the full development setup on each system.

## Check your setup at any time

```bash
reelforge doctor          # Windows: reelforge.cmd doctor
```

It checks Node.js, ffmpeg (version, encoders and filters), Chromium and the bundled fonts, and prints the
exact fix for anything missing. The dashboard shows the same check as the status pill in the top bar.

![reelforge doctor](../screenshots/20-cli-doctor.png)

## Optional speech models

Automatic cue alignment works without any download (pause detection over the known script). For word-level
accuracy with music in the background, install the optional speech models once (about 180 MB):

```bash
reelforge align --setup     # downloads Whisper and Silero VAD into your user cache
reelforge align --status    # shows what is installed
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                        | Fix                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| The dashboard says “setup issues”              | Click the pill: each failed check shows its fix. Most often ffmpeg is missing.                                                             |
| `ffmpeg not found`                             | Windows: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`; macOS: `brew install ffmpeg`; Linux: your package manager. Then open a new terminal or `start.bat`. |
| “Cannot launch Chromium”                       | Run `reelforge doctor --fix`. On Linux, run the installer again and accept the system libraries prompt.                                    |
| ffmpeg installed but still not found (Windows) | Close every terminal and `start.bat`, then reopen: Windows only picks up the new PATH in new windows.                                      |
| `pnpm` is not recognized                       | Run `corepack enable` once (Node.js 22 ships Corepack), then open a new terminal.                                                          |
| Renders are slow or fail with disk errors      | Move the folder out of OneDrive or iCloud and keep about 2 GB free for temporary files.                                                    |

More answers are in [FAQ and troubleshooting](faq.md).

## Updating

If you cloned the repository, run `git pull`, then run the installer again (or `pnpm install && pnpm build`).

If you downloaded a release archive, download the new version from the
[releases page](https://github.com/TerminalDZ/vidcreat/releases), unpack it next to the old one, copy your
`episodes/` folder (and any custom `themes/` or `presets/`) into the new folder, then run the installer
again. Your episodes are plain files: nothing else needs migrating.

## Uninstalling

Delete the ReelForge folder. The Chromium download lives in your user cache folder
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ms-playwright` on Windows, `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright` on macOS,
`~/.cache/ms-playwright` on Linux) and can be deleted too. The optional speech models from
`reelforge align --setup` live in `reelforge` inside the same cache folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\reelforge`,
`~/Library/Caches/reelforge`, `~/.cache/reelforge`).

---

<!-- file: docs/guide/introduction.md -->

# Introduction and concepts

**ReelForge** turns a voice recording and one YAML file into a finished vertical explainer video:
1080×1920 at 30 fps, ready for **TikTok**, **Instagram Reels** and **YouTube Shorts**.

![The ReelForge editor](../screenshots/01-editor-overview.jpg)

You write what you say, sentence by sentence, and describe what appears on screen and **on which word**.
ReelForge animates diagrams, code, tables, charts and titles exactly when you say them, adds word-by-word
captions, sound effects and series branding, masters the audio and encodes platform-ready files.

## Highlights

- **A real editor, made simple.** Place components on the frame like in a design tool, retime them on a
  timeline like in a video editor, edit every property in the inspector, with undo, smart guides,
  a command palette and keyboard shortcuts for everything.
- **Timed to your words.** Elements appear on the word that names them. Re-record a sentence and everything
  after it stays in sync, because animations follow your words, not seconds.
- **English and Arabic.** Word-by-word captions in English, and in Arabic with correct right-to-left layout
  when English terms are mixed in: `الـ client` stays together and `؟` lands on the correct side.
- **Templates for many sectors.** Industry packs (healthcare, real estate, logistics, education, finance and
  more) give you ready templates: fill in a few fields and the episode is designed for you.
- **Works with AI assistants (optional).** A built-in MCP server and a REST API let Claude, Cursor, Copilot,
  Codex, Gemini and other clients write scripts, build scenes and check frames for you.
- **Animated components** for explainers: nodes and arrows with moving packets, code that types itself,
  charts, steps and flows, tables, timelines, meters, counters, a phone mock, stamps…
- **Professional sound**: procedural sound effects on every hit and transition, voice mastered to −14 LUFS
  (the platforms' loudness target), effects ducked under the voice.
- **Platform-ready output**: an archival master MP4, a share MP4 that fits the upload limit you choose,
  SRT captions, a contact sheet and a `publish.md` with your caption, hashtags and pinned comment.
- **No AI in the render engine.** Frames are drawn by a deterministic engine and encoded by FFmpeg. It
  never generates voices or visuals: your voice, your words, your design, consistent every time.
- **Optional local helpers.** Speech alignment marks every line and word from your recording, and scene
  suggestions propose a component for a line. Both run on your computer, and you can always mark cues by
  ear and design scenes yourself instead.
- **Offline and private.** Everything runs on your computer. No account, no subscription, no upload.
  `reelforge align --setup` downloads the optional speech models once; after that, everything runs offline.
- **Deterministic.** The same inputs always produce the same frames.

## Concepts

| Term                | Meaning                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Episode**         | One video: a folder `episodes/<id>/` with `episode.yaml`, your `voice.wav`, `cues.json` and the outputs in `out/`.                               |
| **Script line**     | One spoken sentence. Lines get ids `l1`, `l2`, … in order. Captions are built from them.                                                         |
| **Cue**             | The moment a line starts in your recording. Cues come from automatic alignment, from marking by ear, or from an estimate before you record.      |
| **Scene**           | A group of elements on screen. A scene starts on a line (`at: l3`) and ends where the next scene starts.                                         |
| **Element**         | One component placed in a scene, with props, a box (`place`), and times to enter and exit.                                                       |
| **Component**       | A building block such as `title`, `node`, `arrow`, `code`, `bar-chart` or `steps`. Props are strict and listed in the components reference.      |
| **Time expression** | A time written relative to your words: `l3`, `l3.end`, `l3:'bucket'`, `@scene.end`, plus offsets such as `+0.4`. Words survive re-recording.     |
| **Theme**           | Colors, fonts, sizes and motion tokens in `themes/<name>.theme.yaml`.                                                                            |
| **Preset**          | The platform layout (`tiktok`, `reels`, `shorts`): header, stage and caption positions and the platform's safe zones.                            |
| **Pack, template**  | An industry pack bundles a theme and templates. A template is an episode with named fields (slots) that you fill in.                             |
| **Timeline**        | The compiled episode with every time resolved. It is the only contract between the compiler and the renderer, which keeps the output repeatable. |

## How a video is made

1. **Start** from a template (`reelforge new <id> --pack <pack> --template <template>`), from a blank
   episode (`reelforge new <id>`) or from the dashboard.
2. **Write the script**: one short spoken sentence per line, about 2.3 words per second.
3. **Design scenes** in the editor or in YAML, with each element entering on the word that names it.
4. **Record** your voice. `reelforge align` marks every line and word; you check by ear in Cues mode.
5. **Review**: every check (overlap, safe zones, text overflow, pacing) has a fix hint.
6. **Render** and upload the share file with the texts from `publish.md`.

The [quick start](quick-start.md) walks through these steps in about ten minutes.

## What is in the repository

| Folder / file                                 | Contents                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `install.bat` (`install.ps1`), `install.sh`   | One-command installers for Windows, macOS and Linux          |
| `start.bat`, `start.sh`, `ReelForge.command`  | Open the dashboard                                           |
| `reelforge.cmd`, `reelforge`                  | The command-line interface                                   |
| `examples/season1/`                           | Nine complete example episodes in English (“System Design”)  |
| `examples/season1-arabic/`                    | The same series in Arabic with English technical terms       |
| `examples/promo/intro/`                       | A 45-second ReelForge intro video, a showcase of animations  |
| `packs/`                                      | Industry packs: manifests, templates and example episodes    |
| `skills/`                                     | Task guides for AI assistants (Agent Skills format)          |
| `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, …      | Instructions for AI assistants (see [AI integration](ai.md)) |
| `themes/`, `presets/`                         | Editable visual themes and platform layouts                  |
| `docs/`, `documentation/`                     | This documentation (site source, and an offline copy)        |
| `packages/`                                   | Full TypeScript source code                                  |
| `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` | Apache-2.0 license, notices and third-party credits          |

## Requirements

|                  | Minimum                                                  | Recommended                                             |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Operating system | Windows 10, macOS 13, Ubuntu 22.04 (or any recent Linux) | Windows 11, macOS 14+, Ubuntu 24.04                     |
| CPU / RAM        | 4 cores, 8 GB                                            | 8 threads or more, 16 GB (renders scale with cores)     |
| Disk             | 2 GB free (plus ~2 GB temporary space per render)        | SSD                                                     |
| Software         | **Node.js 22 LTS**, **ffmpeg 6+**                        | installed automatically by the installer where possible |

A 2-minute episode renders in roughly 5–10 minutes on an 8-thread laptop.

| This site: VitePress                        | MIT                                        |

FFmpeg and Chromium are installed separately and are not distributed with ReelForge.

The optional speech models and their runtime (Whisper weights and Silero VAD, both MIT; the model
runtime packages under Apache-2.0, MIT and, for the libvips image library, LGPL-3.0-or-later) are
downloaded once by `reelforge align --setup` into your user cache folder. They are not part of the
ReelForge download.

## Contributing and support

Contributions are welcome under the Apache License 2.0; see [Contributing](contributing.md). For questions,
bug reports and feature requests, see [`SUPPORT.md`](../../SUPPORT.md). Please include your operating
system, the output of `reelforge doctor --json` and the command you ran with `--verbose`.

<!-- file: docs/guide/quick-start.md -->

# Quick start: your first video in 10 minutes

This walk-through makes a 30-second episode from an industry template, previews it without a recording,
then adds your voice and renders. You need ReelForge [installed](installation.md) and `reelforge doctor`
passing. Commands use `reelforge`; on Windows type `reelforge.cmd`, on macOS and Linux `./reelforge`.

## 1. Create an episode from a template (1 minute)

```bash
reelforge new clinic-intro --pack healthcare --template patient-journey --lang en
```

This writes `episodes/clinic-intro/episode.yaml` with a script, scenes and estimated (draft) cues, so the
episode previews immediately. Use `--lang ar` for an Arabic voice-over. The [pack catalog](../reference/packs.md)
lists every pack and template, and the dashboard offers the same choice under **+ New episode** →
**Start from template**.

Prefer a blank start? `reelforge new ep10 --series "SYSTEM DESIGN"` creates a commented template, or click
**+ New episode** in the dashboard (`start.bat` / `./start.sh`).

## 2. Open the editor and make it yours (4 minutes)

```bash
reelforge edit clinic-intro
```

- In the **Script** tab on the left, edit the lines. Keep **one spoken sentence per line**, about
  2.3 words per second. Line 1 is your hook.
- Click an element on the canvas and change its text in the inspector, or double-click to edit in place.
  Words between `**` get the accent color: `**Duplicate** Charge`.
- To make an element appear on a word, put the playhead on that word and click the **target** button next
  to **Enter at**. The editor writes a time such as `l3:'desk'`, which stays on the word after you re-record.
- **Insert** adds a component (or drag one onto the canvas). Drag clips on the timeline to retime them;
  they snap to your words.

Everything is saved to `episode.yaml` as you go, with comments kept.

## 3. Check it (1 minute)

Switch to **Review** (**Alt+3**). Each issue, such as text that overflows or an element under the platform
buttons, comes with a fix hint; click it to jump to the element. From the command line:

```bash
reelforge validate clinic-intro
reelforge snap clinic-intro l1+1 l3+1        # PNG frames in episodes/clinic-intro/out/snaps
```

## 4. Record and align (3 minutes)

Record yourself reading the script with any app (phone, Audacity, OBS…), leaving a short pause between
sentences. In the dashboard click **Upload voice** (WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, OPUS or FLAC are converted to
`voice.wav`), or save the file as `episodes/clinic-intro/voice.wav`. Then mark the cues:

```bash
reelforge align clinic-intro
```

Open **Cues** mode (**Alt+2**), listen through once and fix any line by ear (press **Space** at the start of
a line). [Timing, cues and alignment](timing.md) explains the details.

## 5. Render (1 minute to start)

```bash
reelforge render clinic-intro
```

Or click **Render** (**⌘/Ctrl+Enter**) in the editor. When it finishes, upload
`episodes/clinic-intro/out/clinic-intro.share.mp4` with the caption and hashtags from `out/publish.md`.
No recording yet? `reelforge render clinic-intro --silent` renders a preview with the draft timing.

> Prefer working with an AI assistant? See [AI integration](ai.md). An assistant can write the script,
> build the scenes and check the frames for you through the MCP server.

---

<!-- file: docs/guide/rendering.md -->

# Rendering and publishing

Render from the dashboard (**Render** on a card), the editor (**⌘/Ctrl+Enter**) or the command line. Every
option is listed in the [CLI reference](../reference/cli.md#reelforge-render).

```bash
reelforge render ep10
reelforge render ep10 --preset reels --share-size 50
reelforge render ep10 --from 12 --to 20      # quick partial check → out/ep10.part.mp4
reelforge render --all                       # every episode in episodes/
```

![Render output](../screenshots/22-cli-render.png)

## Outputs (`episodes/<id>/out/`)

| File              | Use                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<id>.master.mp4` | Archival quality: H.264 High, CRF 18, AAC 192 kb/s                              |
| `<id>.share.mp4`  | **Upload this one.** Two-pass encoded to fit the share size (default 28 MB)     |
| `<id>.srt`        | Captions for YouTube or accessibility                                           |
| `<id>.sheet.jpg`  | 12-frame contact sheet for a quick review                                       |
| `publish.md`      | Your cover text, caption, hashtags, pinned comment and chapters, ready to paste |
| `<id>.cover.png`  | Cover image (`reelforge snap <id> <time> --cover`)                              |

Every video is verified after encoding: H.264 High profile, yuv420p, 30 fps constant frame rate, AAC
48 kHz, “fast start” (plays while downloading) and the size limit.

## Options

| Option                           | Meaning                                                   |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--preset tiktok\|reels\|shorts` | Platform layout and safe zones                            |
| `--share-size <MB>`              | Size cap of the share file                                |
| `--workers <n>`                  | Parallel render processes (default: CPU cores − 1)        |
| `--fast`                         | Faster final encoding (slightly larger master)            |
| `--no-sfx`                       | Without sound effects                                     |
| `--silent`                       | Allow rendering without a recording (for previews)        |
| `--no-share`                     | Master only                                               |
| `--lossless`                     | PNG frame capture instead of JPEG (slower, for archiving) |

## Performance

Rendering uses all your cores. Approximate times for a 2-minute episode: 4 cores ≈ 10 min, 8 threads ≈
5–6 min. Press **Ctrl+C** (or **Cancel** in the dashboard) at any time: partial files are removed.

## Before you render

- `reelforge validate <id>` shows **0 errors**, and warnings are fixed or understood (`--strict` fails on
  warnings too, useful in CI).
- Preview a few frames shortly after things enter: `reelforge snap <id> "l3:'bucket'+0.8"`.
- `meta.publish` (cover, caption, hashtags, pinned comment) is filled in; it becomes `publish.md`.
- Phone recording? Set `audio: { denoise: true }` or pass `--denoise`.

## Publishing

`publish.md` collects everything you paste when uploading: the cover text, caption, hashtags, pinned
comment and chapter timestamps. Make a cover image with `reelforge snap <id> <time> --cover`.

- **TikTok**: upload `share.mp4`; paste the caption and hashtags from `publish.md`.
- **Instagram Reels**: render with `--preset reels` for its safe zones.
- **YouTube Shorts**: render with `--preset shorts` (max 3 minutes); upload `<id>.srt` as subtitles.

## Rendering on a server or in CI

Everything works headless on Linux. `--json` prints machine-readable progress events, exit codes are
stable (`0` success, `1` failure, `2` usage error), and rendering needs no network once Chromium and
FFmpeg are installed. Render a whole folder with `reelforge render --all`.

---

<!-- file: docs/guide/templates-and-packs.md -->

# Templates and packs

An **industry pack** bundles what one sector needs: a theme, two or three **templates**, recommended scene
blueprints, an example episode in English and Arabic, and a playbook for AI assistants. A template is a
complete episode (script, scenes, timing) with named fields, called **slots**, such as an organization
name, a number or a call-to-action keyword. Filling the slots gives a valid, designed episode in seconds;
you then refine it like any other episode.

The [pack catalog](../reference/packs.md) lists every pack, template and slot, generated from the files in
`packs/`.

## Create an episode from a template

From the command line:

```bash
reelforge packs                      # every pack and template with its slots (--json for details)
reelforge new first-visit --pack healthcare --template patient-journey --lang en \
  --slot "org=Northwind Hospital" --slot wait=10
```

`--lang ar` uses the Arabic version of the template. `--slot key=value` can be repeated; slots you leave
out keep their defaults, and a value that is too long or out of range is rejected before anything is
written. Without `--template` the pack's first template is used. The episode gets draft cues, so it
previews immediately (`reelforge snap first-visit --every 5`); change the texts in the editor or in
`episode.yaml`.

From the dashboard, click **+ New episode** and choose **Start from template**: pick a pack and a
template, fill in the fields (text fields show their length limit, numbers their range, and every field
starts with its default), choose the language and click **Create**.

From an AI assistant, the Tier 1 tools do the same: `list_templates` returns the templates with their
slots, and `create_from_template` takes the episode id, pack, template, language and a flat object of slot
values:

```json
{
  "id": "first-visit",
  "pack": "healthcare",
  "template": "patient-journey",
  "lang": "en",
  "slots": { "org": "Northwind Hospital", "wait": 10, "keyword": "VISIT" }
}
```

## Slots

| Slot type | Value                                  | Limits                       |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `text`    | a short text (default type)            | `max` characters             |
| `number`  | a number                               | `min` and `max` values       |
| `color`   | a theme color name (`lime`, `cyan`, …) | must be a theme color or CSS |

Missing slots keep their defaults, which exist in both languages. Respect the length limits: text that is
too long is the most common cause of V-9 (text overflows its box).

## Scene blueprints

Blueprints are named, parameterized scenes used by the `add_scene` tool (Tier 2) and by the templates:
`hook`, `problem-solution`, `stat-reveal`, `comparison`, `process-steps`, `timeline`, `before-after`,
`bar-stats`, `quote`, `cta`, `map-route`, `appointment` and `chat` (13 in all). Each turns a few flat fields
into positioned elements that enter on the right words. `list_blueprints` returns their fields.

## Example episodes

Each pack has an example in English and Arabic under `packs/<pack>/examples/`. Open one in the editor or
render it without a recording:

```bash
reelforge edit packs/healthcare/examples/first-visit-en
reelforge render packs/healthcare/examples/first-visit-ar --silent
```

## Tutorials by sector

Each [tutorial](tutorials/index.md) makes one short video with one pack, with the tone and compliance
notes for that sector.

## Make your own pack

Packs are plain files: a `pack.yaml` manifest validated when it is loaded, and one template file per
language with `{{slot}}` placeholders. A project can add its own packs in `<project>/packs/`; a pack with
the same id as a bundled one replaces it. See [Contributing](contributing.md#add-an-industry-pack).

```yaml
# <project>/packs/clinic/pack.yaml
id: clinic
name: { en: My clinic, ar: عيادتي }
description: { en: Patient guides, ar: أدلة للمرضى }
theme: clinical
templates:
  - id: first-visit
    title: { en: First visit, ar: الزيارة الأولى }
    description: { en: What happens at a first visit, ar: ماذا يحدث في الزيارة الأولى }
    slots:
      org: { label: Clinic name, max: 26, default: { en: Lakeside Clinic, ar: عيادة ليكسايد } }
      wait: { label: Check-in minutes, type: number, min: 1, max: 120, default: 10 }
    files: { en: templates/first-visit.en.yaml, ar: templates/first-visit.ar.yaml }
```

The easiest way to write a template is to copy a finished episode and replace the parts that change:

- Put text slots inside single-quoted YAML strings (`text: 'Welcome to {{org}}'`); values are escaped for
  them. Numbers go unquoted (`value: {{wait}}`). `{{id}}` is the episode id (`meta.id: '{{id}}'`).
- Anchor entrances on words that are **not** slots (`"l2:'bring'"`), or on line starts and offsets
  (`l2+0.4`): a slot value may not contain the word you anchored on.
- Size every text box for the slot's `max` length, and give every script line something that enters
  while it is spoken.
- Check it with `reelforge new test --pack <your-pack> --slot org=<a long name>` and
  `reelforge validate test`, in both languages. Template files are excluded from Prettier, because they
  are not valid YAML until they are filled.

---

<!-- file: docs/guide/themes.md -->

# Themes and branding

A series looks consistent when its colors, fonts and motion live in one theme instead of in every
element. This page covers themes, fonts, contrast rules for a brand and the platform presets.

## Themes

A theme (`themes/<name>.theme.yaml`) holds every color, font size and motion token. Episodes choose one
with `meta.theme`. A theme can `extends:` another and override only what changes:

```yaml
name: myseries
extends: default
colors:
  lime: '#3cc8ff' # the accent color (titles, active caption word)
  bg: '#070c0e'
chrome: { grain: 0.05, waveform: true }
captions: { active: lime, english: cyan, max_chars: 34 }
```

| Group      | Tokens                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mode`     | `dark` (default) or `light`. Light themes get dark hairlines, soft shadows and light component surfaces (phone, trap, labels) |
| `colors`   | `bg ink dim line card lime cyan red amber violet` (add your own names freely)                                                 |
| `fonts`    | `display` (Space Grotesk), `mono` (JetBrains Mono), `arabic` (Cairo); any bundled font, see below                             |
| `type`     | font sizes: `caption title h2 body label`                                                                                     |
| `chrome`   | `header progress waveform grid` (on/off), `grain` (0–1), `grain_fps` (0 = static), `vignette` (0–1), `glow` (0–1, default 1)  |
| `motion`   | `pop_overshoot default_dur crossfade`                                                                                         |
| `captions` | `active english` colors, `future_opacity`, `max_lines`, `max_chars`, `scrim`                                                  |

The color tokens carry meaning: `lime` is the primary accent and "ok", `red` is errors, `amber` is
warnings, `cyan` is info. Keep each one in its family when you rebrand.

### Bundled themes

| Theme        | Mode  | For                        | Fonts (display · arabic)             |
| ------------ | ----- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `default`    | dark  | tech explainers (Season 1) | Space Grotesk · Cairo                |
| `season1`    | dark  | same as default            | Space Grotesk · Cairo                |
| `workshop`   | dark  | courses                    | Space Grotesk · Cairo                |
| `clinical`   | light | healthcare                 | Inter · Readex Pro                   |
| `estate`     | light | real estate                | Playfair Display · Noto Naskh Arabic |
| `campus`     | light | education                  | Manrope · Readex Pro                 |
| `civic`      | light | public services            | Inter · Noto Kufi Arabic             |
| `minimal`    | light | anything, quiet            | Inter · Readex Pro                   |
| `harbor`     | dark  | ports and logistics        | Manrope · Noto Kufi Arabic           |
| `ledger`     | dark  | finance                    | Inter · Noto Kufi Arabic             |
| `bistro`     | dark  | food and restaurants       | Playfair Display · Noto Naskh Arabic |
| `retail`     | dark  | shops and offers           | Manrope · Cairo                      |
| `industrial` | dark  | manufacturing, engineering | Space Grotesk · Noto Kufi Arabic     |
| `voyage`     | dark  | travel and tourism         | Manrope · Readex Pro                 |
| `editorial`  | dark  | news                       | Playfair Display · Noto Naskh Arabic |
| `bold`       | dark  | social promos              | Manrope · Cairo                      |

Every bundled theme passes WCAG AA: `ink`, `dim`, the five accents and both caption colors reach
at least 4.5:1 on `bg` and on `card`, and caption colors reach 7:1 on the background
(`packages/core/test/themes.test.ts`).

### Fonts

All fonts are bundled with the runtime (SIL Open Font License 1.1, no network at render time).
`fonts` must name one of them (V-13):

| Slot      | Families                                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `display` | Space Grotesk, Inter, Manrope, Playfair Display (serif)                         |
| `mono`    | JetBrains Mono                                                                  |
| `arabic`  | Cairo, Noto Kufi Arabic, Noto Naskh Arabic (naskh), Readex Pro (Latin + Arabic) |

Captions use the `arabic` font first, so pick one whose Latin letters also suit English captions.

### Generate a theme

```bash
reelforge theme new myseries --accent "#3cc8ff"
reelforge theme new clinic --accent "#00a884" --mode light --font "Noto Kufi Arabic"
```

| Option           | Meaning                                                                                |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--accent <hex>` | primary accent (`lime`); kept as is when readable, otherwise its lightness is adjusted |
| `--mode <mode>`  | `dark` (default) or `light`                                                            |
| `--font <name>`  | a bundled family; it goes into its own slot (display, mono or arabic)                  |
| `--out <file>`   | write somewhere other than `themes/<name>.theme.yaml`                                  |

The generator writes every color token and checks the same WCAG AA rules as the bundled themes.

ReelForge warns when a caption color has less than 7:1 contrast against the background.

## Brand a series

1. Generate a theme from the brand's primary color: `reelforge theme new acme --accent "#2f7dff"`.
2. Map the brand onto the tokens: `lime` is the accent (accent words in titles, the active caption word),
   `cyan` the secondary accent; `bg`, `card`, `line`, `ink` and `dim` are the neutrals.
3. If the brand font is not bundled, pick the closest bundled family. System and web fonts are not
   allowed, because renders must not depend on the machine.
4. Set `meta.theme: acme` in every episode of the series, then validate and preview frames in each scene's
   glow color.

| Text                                                            | Minimum contrast against its background |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Body text, labels, chips                                        | 4.5:1                                   |
| Large text: titles, counters (≥ 24 px, or ≥ 18.66 px bold)      | 3:1                                     |
| Captions (`ink`, `captions.active`, `captions.english` vs `bg`) | 7:1 (ReelForge warns below)             |

Check accent text on `bg` **and** on `card`, since chips and nodes sit on cards. Never carry meaning in
color alone: pair red and green with an icon, a label or a strike. Industry packs ship a matching theme
for each sector (see [Templates and packs](templates-and-packs.md)).

## Platform presets

`presets/tiktok.preset.yaml`, `reels.preset.yaml` and `shorts.preset.yaml` define the header, stage and
caption positions, the safe-zone rectangles, the default share size and the maximum duration. Edit them
freely or add your own (`presets/<name>.preset.yaml`), then select it with `meta.preset` or
`--preset` when rendering.

---

<!-- file: docs/guide/timing.md -->

# Timing, cues and auto alignment

Everything in an episode is timed relative to your words. A **cue** is the moment a script line starts in
your recording; word times follow from it. Scenes start on lines and elements enter on words:

```yaml
scenes:
  - at: l3 # the scene starts with line 3
    elements:
      - use: bucket
        enter: { at: "l3:'bucket'" } # the element enters on the word "bucket"
```

Re-record a sentence, move its cue, and every animation follows.

## Time expressions

| Form                              | Meaning                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `12.5s` (or a YAML number `12.5`) | absolute seconds                                                            |
| `l7`                              | cue start of line `l7`                                                      |
| `l7.end`                          | start of the next line − 0.15 s                                             |
| `l7:'timeout'`                    | first word matching "timeout" (punctuation, tatweel and diacritics ignored) |
| `l7:'request'#2`                  | second match                                                                |
| `l7.3`                            | the 4th word (0-based)                                                      |
| `@hook`, `@hook.end`              | a scene's start / end                                                       |
| any of the above `+0.4` / `-0.2`  | offset in seconds                                                           |

Quote YAML strings that contain `:` or `'`, for example `at: "l3:'bucket'"`. Prefer word expressions to
absolute seconds: words survive re-recording. The full list is in [Writing episodes](../authoring.md).

## Before you record: draft cues

A new episode gets **draft cues**, estimated from the length of each line (about 13 characters per second
plus a short gap). The preview plays with realistic timing, and validation already checks pacing. Write them
with `reelforge cue <id> --draft`, the **Draft cues** button, or the `draft_cues` tool.

## Recording tips

- Record in a quiet room, 20–30 cm from the microphone. Any sample rate works; ReelForge masters the
  loudness for you (−14 LUFS).
- Read one script line per breath and leave a short pause (0.3–0.5 s) between lines. Pauses make marking
  faster and give animations room.
- Re-recording later? Upload the new take: ReelForge warns that the voice changed so you can re-check the
  cues.
- Recorded on a phone or in a noisy room? Turn on **Clean up noise** (episode settings, or
  `audio: { denoise: true }`, or `reelforge render --denoise`). RNNoise removes hiss, hum and room noise
  from the voice before mastering; in tests it lowers the noise between sentences by about 15 dB without
  changing the voice level.

## Automatic cues

Click **Auto-mark from voice** in Cues mode, **Auto cues** on the dashboard, or run
`reelforge align <id>`. ReelForge already knows the script, so it only has to find where each line and
each word starts in the recording. Then listen through once and fix any line by ear (amber lines are the
ones it was least sure about). The result is one undo step (**⌘/Ctrl+Z**).

Two engines:

| Engine                 | Needs                                    | Speed (1 min of voice) | How it works                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Pauses** (default)   | nothing                                  | ~0.05 s                | Finds the pauses, then splits the recording into the script's lines so each line's length matches its text (dynamic programming). Words follow the syllables.          |
| **Whisper** (optional) | `reelforge align --setup` once (~180 MB) | ~20 s on a laptop CPU  | A speech model hears the words; only its **timings** are used, matched to your script, so dialects and English terms in Arabic don't matter. Best for words and music. |

With the optional models installed, a 2 MB voice-activity model (Silero VAD) also tells speech from
music, breaths and room noise. Measured on recorded speech with known timings, every line lands within
100 ms (average 15 ms), with or without background music. Words land within 100 ms about 80% of the time,
so give precise hits (a stamp on one exact word) a listen in word mode.

`reelforge align --status` shows what is installed. Models live in your user cache
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\reelforge`, `~/Library/Caches/reelforge` or `~/.cache/reelforge`; `$REELFORGE_CACHE`
moves it) and are never used while rendering. Cues you marked by hand are never replaced unless you
confirm (`--force` on the command line).

| Option           | Meaning                                                          |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--engine <e>`   | `auto` (Whisper when installed, else pauses), `dsp` or `whisper` |
| `--model <size>` | Whisper model: `tiny`, `base` (default) or `small`               |
| `--no-vad`       | Detect speech by energy only                                     |
| `--no-words`     | Line cues only                                                   |
| `--force`        | Replace cues you marked by hand                                  |
| `--dry-run`      | Print the result without writing `cues.json`                     |

## Cues mode

Open the editor and switch to **Cues** (**Alt+2**), or click **Mark cues** on the dashboard. The script
is listed on the right, the playhead and waveform are on the timeline.

![Cues mode](../screenshots/07-editor-cues.jpg)

| Key                           | Action                                                              |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Enter** / **K**             | Play / pause                                                        |
| **1 / 2 / 3**                 | Speed 0.5× / 0.75× / 1× (slower = more accurate)                    |
| **Space**                     | Mark the next unmarked line at the playhead                         |
| **Click a line** or **↑ / ↓** | Select a line to re-mark it (then press Space)                      |
| **← / →**                     | Nudge the selected cue by 50 ms (**Shift**: 10 ms)                  |
| **Backspace**                 | Undo the last change                                                |
| **S** / **A**                 | Snap the selected cue to the nearest voice onset / toggle auto-snap |
| **G**                         | Jump to the selected cue                                            |
| **W**                         | Word mode: mark each word of the selected line with Space           |
| **J / L**, **, / .**          | Back / forward 1 s, previous / next frame                           |

Every change is saved instantly to `cues.json` and can be undone with **⌘/Ctrl+Z**. Lines out of order
are shown in red. You can also drag a line's clip on the **Script** track of the timeline, in Edit or
Cues mode.

## Word mode

By default ReelForge estimates when each word starts from its length. For precise hits (a stamp landing
exactly on “twice”), select the line, press **W**, play, and press **Space** on each word.

![Word mode](../screenshots/08-editor-cues-word-mode.jpg)

## Pacing checks

Validation rule **V-14** warns when a line is spoken faster than about 3.5 words per second (too fast to
read in captions) and when the hook starts after 3 s; it also reports silences of 1.5 s or more. Split long
lines, or slow down when you record.

---

<!-- file: docs/guide/tutorials/education.md -->

# Education tutorial

You will make one concept explained in 45 seconds, with the `education` pack and its `campus` theme. Allow about ten minutes
before recording.

## 1. Create the episode

```bash
reelforge new concept-45s --pack education --template concept-explainer --lang en
```

Use `--lang ar` for an Arabic version. The pack also has `study-plan` and `enrollment-steps`. The [pack catalog](../../reference/packs.md#education) lists
every template and its slots.

## 2. Fill in your details

Open the episode with `reelforge edit concept-45s` and replace the default names, numbers and keyword with
your own, or start from the dashboard (**+ New episode** → **Start from template**), whose form asks for each field. Keep within
the length limits shown for each slot.

**Audience and tone.** Students, parents and teachers. Be encouraging and clear, with one concept per episode.

- Open with a question the viewer has asked themselves.
- Build the idea step by step with `steps` or `tree`, one element per spoken idea.
- Close with a short recap or a question for the comments.

## 3. Check the content

- Definitions and formulas must be correct; check them before recording.
- No real exam papers, teachers or schools.
- Content for minors: no requests for personal data and no links to off-platform chats.

## 4. Validate, record and render

```bash
reelforge validate concept-45s
reelforge align concept-45s          # after you save voice.wav in the episode folder
reelforge render concept-45s
```

<!-- file: docs/guide/tutorials/index.md -->

# Tutorials

Each tutorial makes one short video with one [industry pack](../templates-and-packs.md): create the episode
from a template, fill in your details, check the sector's content rules, then validate, record and render.
New to ReelForge? Do the [quick start](../quick-start.md) first.

| Tutorial                                  | Pack              | Theme        | You will make                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Healthcare](healthcare.md)               | `healthcare`      | `clinical`   | A 30-second guide to a first visit at a fictional hospital            |
| [Real estate](real-estate.md)             | `real-estate`     | `estate`     | A short tour of an apartment for a fictional agency                   |
| [Ports and logistics](ports-logistics.md) | `ports-logistics` | `harbor`     | The journey of a container from ship to truck at a fictional port     |
| [Education](education.md)                 | `education`       | `campus`     | One concept explained in 45 seconds                                   |
| [Finance](finance.md)                     | `finance`         | `ledger`     | How a simple monthly budget works                                     |
| [Food and hospitality](food.md)           | `food`            | `bistro`     | A signature dish made in four steps at a fictional restaurant         |
| [Retail](retail.md)                       | `retail`          | `retail`     | How click-and-collect works at a fictional shop                       |
| [Government services](government.md)      | `government`      | `civic`      | How residents of a fictional city renew a document online             |
| [Tourism and travel](tourism.md)          | `tourism`         | `voyage`     | A three-day itinerary for a fictional coastal town                    |
| [Manufacturing](manufacturing.md)         | `manufacturing`   | `industrial` | How a part is made at a fictional plant, from raw material to the box |
| [Events and non-profits](events-ngo.md)   | `events-ngo`      | `editorial`  | A call for volunteers for a beach clean-up day                        |
| [Tech and software](tech.md)              | `tech`            | `default`    | Rate limiting with a token bucket, for backend developers             |

Every tutorial uses fictional organizations. The content rules come from the industry playbooks in
`skills/reelforge-industry-playbooks/`, which AI assistants follow as well.

# Manufacturing tutorial

You will make how a part is made at a fictional plant, from raw material to the box, with the `manufacturing` pack and its `industrial` theme. Allow about ten minutes
before recording.

the length limits shown for each slot.

**Audience and tone.** Operators, technicians, buyers and recruits. Be precise and safety-first.

- Show the stages as a `flow` with a moving token, one stage per spoken step.
