<!-- file: skills/reelforge-brand-and-themes/SKILL.md -->

# Brand and themes

A theme (`themes/<name>.theme.yaml`) holds every color, font, size and motion token. Episodes pick
one with `meta.theme`. Never hard-code brand colors into every element; put them in the theme.

## Create a theme from brand colors

1. Generate a starting point:

   ```bash
   ./reelforge theme new acme --accent "#2f7dff" --font "Space Grotesk" --mode dark
   ```

   `--accent` is the brand's primary color; `--mode light|dark` chooses the background family;
   `--font` must be a bundled font. Older builds accept only `--accent`; then set the rest by hand.

2. Map the brand onto tokens: `lime` is the **accent** token (titles' `**accent**` words, the active
   caption word), `cyan` the secondary accent and English terms in Arabic captions; `bg`, `card`,
   `line`, `ink`, `dim` are the neutrals.
3. Check contrast (below), set `meta.theme: acme`, `validate_episode`, `preview_frames`.

Ready-made themes may exist for common industries (`clinical`, `estate`, `harbor`, `campus`,
`ledger`, `bistro`, `civic`, `retail`, `industrial`, `voyage`, `editorial`, `minimal`, `bold`,
`default`). If `validate_episode` reports "Theme not found" (V-1), use `default` or create it.

## Fonts

Only fonts bundled with ReelForge (OFL-licensed, embedded for deterministic rendering) are
allowed. An unknown font is error V-13, whose hint lists the bundled families. The base set is
`Space Grotesk` (display), `JetBrains Mono` (mono) and `Cairo` (Arabic). If the brand font is not
bundled, pick the closest bundled family and tell the person; do not reference system or web fonts.

## Contrast rules (WCAG AA)

| Text                                                            | Minimum ratio against its background |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Body text, labels, chips (< 24 px bold / < 18.66 px)            | 4.5:1                                |
| Large text: titles, counters (≥ 24 px, or ≥ 18.66 px bold)      | 3:1                                  |
| Captions (`ink`, `captions.active`, `captions.english` vs `bg`) | 7:1 (ReelForge warns below)          |

- Check accent text on `bg` **and** on `card` (chips and nodes sit on cards).
- Light mode: dark `ink` on a light `bg`; brand colors usually need a darker shade to reach 4.5:1.
- Never put meaning in color alone: pair red/green with an icon, a label or a strike.

## Good and bad

Good: extends the default, overrides only what the brand changes, keeps caption contrast.

```yaml
name: acme
extends: default
colors:
  bg: '#0a0f1c'
  card: '#121a2e'
  line: '#24304d'
  lime: '#66adff' # brand accent, lightened: 8.2:1 on bg, 7.4:1 on card
  cyan: '#7ee0c3'
fonts: { display: 'Space Grotesk' }
chrome: { grain: 0.04 }
captions: { active: lime, english: cyan }
```

Bad: a font that is not bundled, low-contrast accent, unknown keys.

```yaml
name: acme
colors:
  bg: '#ffffff'
  lime: '#ffd400' # 1.4:1 on white
fonts: { display: 'Helvetica Neue' }
logo: brand.png
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Theme `extends: default` (or another theme) and overrides only brand tokens.
- [ ] Fonts are bundled families only (no V-13).
- [ ] Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1, large text ≥ 3:1, captions ≥ 7:1 (no contrast warning).
- [ ] Accent tested on both `bg` and `card`.
- [ ] `meta.theme` set; preview frames checked in every scene's glow color.

References: [theme-tokens](references/theme-tokens.md), [contrast](references/contrast.md).

---

<!-- file: skills/reelforge-contribute-component/SKILL.md -->

# Contribute a component

A component is a contract in two halves: a **Zod schema with defaults** in `@reelforge/core`
(validated at compile time) and a **pure renderer** in `@reelforge/runtime` (drawn at time `t` in
Chromium). The compiled Timeline is the only thing passed between them.

## Files to touch, in order

1. **Schema** in `packages/core/src/components/`: props in `schemas.ts` (text, diagrams) or
   `visual.ts` (data and structure), reusing `fragments.ts` (`valueKeyframes`, `numberFormat`,
   `stagger`, `animDur`, `fontSize`, `datum`, `focus`, `treeNodes`). Every object `.strict()`,
   sensible `.default()`s, sizes bounded (`.min()`/`.max()` on arrays).
2. **Registry** entry in `packages/core/src/components/index.ts` (`COMPONENTS`): `name`, `schema`,
   one-line `description`, default `size`, `layer`, `enter`, `endpoints`/`fill` if relevant, and
   `events` for default sounds (use `itemTime`/`itemEvents` so sounds match the runtime schedule).
3. **Runtime** in `packages/runtime/src/components/<group>.ts` implementing `RuntimeComponent`
   (`name`, `mount(root, props, theme, ctx)` returning `{ update(t, local, state) }`), and list it
   in `COMPONENT_REGISTRY` (`packages/runtime/src/components/index.ts`). Styles in
   `packages/runtime/src/styles.ts`.
4. **Gallery**: a scene for it in `fixtures/golden/components/episode.yaml` (and its cue in
   `cues.json`) showing the default look and the main options.
5. **Docs**: `node scripts/gen-components-doc.mjs` regenerates `docs/components.md`; mention it in
   `AGENTS.md` only if the component list there changes.
6. **Studio**: a valid, good-looking default in `starterProps()`
   (`packages/studio/client/src/actions.ts`) so the editor's insert gives a useful element.
7. Optional: a keyword rule in `packages/core/src/suggest.ts` so `suggest_scene` proposes it.
8. **Golden frames**: `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 pnpm test:browser`, then inspect the new PNGs before
   committing them.

Details per step: [files](references/files.md).

## Determinism rules

- `update(t, …)` is a pure function of `t`, props, theme and resolved state. No `Date.now()`,
  `performance.now()`, `Math.random()` (use `ctx.seed` and `local.frame` for seeded jitter), no
  timers, no `requestAnimationFrame`, no CSS transitions or animations that run on their own.
- Seeking backwards must produce the same frame as playing forward: never accumulate state across
  `update` calls; derive everything from `t`.
- Reuse the helpers in `packages/runtime/src/components/util.ts` (`fitText`, `fontFor`,
  `parseAccent`, `keyframeValue`, `statusColor`, `Reveal`) instead of re-implementing them. Load
  nothing over the network; assets come through `ctx.asset()`.
- Support right-to-left text (`isArabic`, `fontFor`) wherever a prop holds user text.
- Times in props are already resolved to seconds by the compiler for keys named `at`/`until`; do
  not parse expressions in the runtime.

More: [determinism-and-tests](references/determinism-and-tests.md).

## Good and bad schema

Good: strict, defaults, bounded, theme color names, time keys named `at`.

```ts
export const gaugeProps = z
  .object({
    value: z.number(),
    max: z.number().positive().default(100),
    label: z.string().optional(),
    keyframes: valueKeyframes().optional(),
    color: color().default('lime'),
    dur: animDur(1.0),
  })
  .strict();
```

Bad: loose object, unbounded arrays, hex-only colors, a time key the compiler will not resolve.

```ts
export const gaugeProps = z.object({
  value: z.any(),
  ticks: z.array(z.number()),
  hex: z.string().regex(/^#/),
  startTime: z.string(),
});
```

Gallery entry (valid episode YAML):

```yaml
scenes:
  - id: stat_card
    at: l12
    elements:
      - use: stat-card
        id: kpi
        props: { label: 'On-time arrivals', value: 92, suffix: '%', delta: 4 }
        place: { x: 330, y: 300, w: 420, h: 260 }
        enter: { at: l12, anim: rise }
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Schema strict with defaults; registry entry with description, size, layer, enter, events.
- [ ] Runtime registered; `update(t)` pure and deterministic (seek test passes).
- [ ] Gallery scene added; golden frames regenerated and inspected.
- [ ] `docs/components.md` regenerated; studio `starterProps` added.
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test:unit` pass; `pnpm test:browser` passes.
- [ ] No test weakened to make it pass.

---

<!-- file: skills/reelforge-industry-playbooks/SKILL.md -->

# Industry playbooks

Each industry has its own audience, vocabulary and limits. Read the matching reference before
writing the script; it lists typical episodes, the blueprints and components that fit, the theme
and the compliance rules.

## How to use a playbook

1. Identify the industry from the request and load its reference:
   `get_guide reelforge-industry-playbooks/<industry>` (for example `…/healthcare`).
2. Take the audience and tone into the script (`reelforge-script-writing`).
3. Pick an episode type from the playbook and its blueprint (Tier 2) or a template whose name or
   description matches the industry (Tier 1, `list_templates`).
4. Set `meta.theme` to the suggested theme; if it is not installed (V-1 "Theme not found"), use
   `default` or create it (`reelforge-brand-and-themes`).
5. Apply the compliance notes before you validate; they are not optional.

| Industry           | Reference                                        | Theme        |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------ |
| Healthcare         | [healthcare](references/healthcare.md)           | `clinical`   |
| Real estate        | [real-estate](references/real-estate.md)         | `estate`     |
| Ports & logistics  | [ports-logistics](references/ports-logistics.md) | `harbor`     |
| Education          | [education](references/education.md)             | `campus`     |
| Finance            | [finance](references/finance.md)                 | `ledger`     |
| Food & hospitality | [food](references/food.md)                       | `bistro`     |
| Retail             | [retail](references/retail.md)                   | `retail`     |
| Government         | [government](references/government.md)           | `civic`      |
| Tourism            | [tourism](references/tourism.md)                 | `voyage`     |
| Manufacturing      | [manufacturing](references/manufacturing.md)     | `industrial` |
| Events & NGOs      | [events-ngo](references/events-ngo.md)           | `editorial`  |
| Tech               | [tech](references/tech.md)                       | `default`    |

Neutral alternatives for any industry: `minimal` (calm, few effects) and `bold` (high energy).

## Rules for every industry

- **No real brands, people or organizations.** Use fictional ones: "Northwind Hospital", "Port of
  Azur", "Cedar Homes", "Brightway Bank", "Maple Street Bistro". Logos only from the person's own
  `assets/`.
- **No professional advice**: no diagnosis, treatment, dosage, investment, tax or legal advice.
  Explain how things work and point to a qualified professional.
- **Numbers must come from the person** or be clearly illustrative ("for example, 5 days"). Never
  invent statistics presented as facts.
- **No guarantees** ("always", "100%", "risk-free") and no before/after claims about health or
  money.
- **Inclusive and respectful** wording; no stereotypes in examples or icons.

## Good and bad

Good: fictional organization, explains a process, sends to a professional.

```yaml
script:
  - text: 'What happens after you check in at Northwind Hospital?'
  - text: 'A nurse records your vital signs first.'
  - text: 'Questions about your results? Ask your care team.'
```

Bad: a real-sounding brand, a medical claim and advice.

```yaml
script:
  - text: 'This supplement cures migraines in three days, guaranteed.'
  - text: 'Stop your medication and try it instead.'
```

## Checklist

- [ ] The industry reference was read; tone and audience match it.
- [ ] Only fictional organizations, people and products appear (script, props, publish).
- [ ] No advice, diagnosis, guarantees or invented statistics.
- [ ] Theme set (or `default` with a note to the person).
- [ ] Compliance notes from the reference applied; disclaimers where the reference asks for them.

---

<!-- file: skills/reelforge-make-video/SKILL.md -->

# Make a ReelForge video end to end

A ReelForge video is one `episodes/<id>/episode.yaml` plus a voice recording. You write the script
and the scenes; ReelForge renders 1080×1920 frames deterministically. You never render audio or
voices yourself: the person records `voice.wav`.

## Quick path

1. **Pick your tier** (below) and stay in it. Lower tiers are safer; move up only when a tier
   cannot express what you need.
2. **Script**: 6–14 short lines, hook first, CTA last, about 2.3 words/s
   (`get_guide reelforge-script-writing`).
3. **Create** the episode (template, script or YAML, depending on the tier).
4. **Design** 4–7 scenes, one idea each, elements entering on the word that names them.
5. **Validate**, read `fixes`, apply them, repeat until 0 errors.
6. **Preview** frames shortly after things enter and fix what you see.
7. **Hand over**: the person records, runs `align_cues`, listens once, renders.

## Pick a tool tier

| Tier | Fits                                     | Tools                                                                           | You write                             |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Small models, short context, weak YAML   | `list_templates`, `create_from_template` (flat slots), `suggest_scenes`         | Plain strings and numbers only        |
| 2    | Medium models                            | `create_episode` + `add_scene` with a named blueprint, `suggest_scene` per line | One scene at a time as flat fields    |
| 3    | Strong models that read schemas reliably | `edit_episode` (set/insert/delete/move by path), `write_episode_yaml`           | Any valid YAML, any of the components |

Blueprints for `add_scene`: `hook`, `problem-solution`, `stat-reveal`, `comparison`,
`process-steps`, `timeline`, `map-route`, `before-after`, `quote`, `cta`. Every tier shares
`validate_episode`, `preview_frames`, `get_episode` and the render tools. Details and call shapes:
[tool-tiers](references/tool-tiers.md).

Rules of thumb:

- Unsure? Start at Tier 1 and only use `edit_episode` for the specific fixes listed in `fixes`.
- Tier 2 output can be refined with Tier 3 edits; never the reverse (do not call
  `create_from_template` on an episode you have hand-edited).
- Tool names and arguments follow semver. Read each tool's input schema before the first call.

## Entry points

- **MCP stdio** (preferred): `node packages/cli/bin/reelforge.js mcp` (configured in `.mcp.json`).
  Limit the tool list for small models: `--toolsets basic` or `basic,design`.
- **MCP over HTTP / REST**: `reelforge studio`, then `/mcp`, or `POST /api/v1/tools/<name>` with JSON
  arguments (`GET /api/v1/openapi.json` for function calling).
- **CLI only**: `reelforge new`, `cue --draft`, `validate --json`, `snap`, `render`.

See [entry-points](references/entry-points.md) for exact commands and payloads.

## The validate → preview → fix loop

Every write tool returns `issues` (`errors`, `warnings`, `list`), `fixes` (one hint per problem) and
`next` (the recommended next step). Follow `next` literally unless you have a reason not to.

```text
loop (max 6 rounds):
  result = <write tool>(...)
  if result.issues.errors > 0: apply each entry of result.fixes, continue
  frames = preview_frames(times shortly after each scene's main element enters)
  if a frame shows overlap, overflow, platform UI hits or empty space: fix, continue
  break
```

If the same error comes back twice, change approach (move the element, shorten the text, split the
scene) instead of nudging the same value again. Explain any warning you deliberately keep.

## Good and bad

Good: one idea per scene, the element enters on the word that names it.

```yaml
scenes:
  - id: limit
    at: l3
    glow: cyan
    elements:
      - use: counter
        id: rps
        props: { from: 0, keyframes: [{ at: "l3:'thousand'", value: 1000, dur: 1 }], suffix: ' req/s' }
        place: { x: 140, y: 180, w: 800, h: 300 }
        enter: { at: "l3:'thousand'", anim: pop }
```

Bad: absolute seconds, several unrelated ideas, the text box pushed into the right rail.

```yaml
scenes:
  - id: everything
    at: l3
    elements:
      - use: title
        props: { text: 'Rate limits, retries, queues and caches explained' }
        place: { x: 300, y: 700, w: 760, h: 240 }
        enter: { at: 14.2s }
```

## Checklist

- [ ] The tier fits the model; every tool call matches its input schema.
- [ ] Script: hook in line 1, one idea per line, CTA last, ≤ 3.5 words/s (V-14).
- [ ] `validate_episode`: 0 errors; warnings fixed or explained.
- [ ] `preview_frames` checked at least once per scene (images, or the layout text).
- [ ] `meta.publish` filled in (cover, caption, hashtags, pinned).
- [ ] The person knows the next step: record `voice.wav`, `align_cues`, listen, render.

More: [full-example](references/full-example.md) is a complete episode that validates.

---

<!-- file: skills/reelforge-review-and-render/SKILL.md -->

# Review and render

Rendering takes minutes; review takes seconds. Review first, render once.

## Review loop

1. `validate_episode` → fix every error; fix or explain every warning. Each result carries `fixes`
   (one hint per problem) and `next`.
2. `preview_frames` at the moments that matter (up to 8 per call):
   - each scene's hero shortly after it enters: `"l3:'bucket'+0.8"`;
   - the busiest moment of each scene (most elements visible);
   - the hook at about 1 s and the CTA at its end.
3. Fix, then preview the same times again to confirm.
4. Only when validate is clean and frames look right: render.

Vision models look at the images. **Text-only models** read the layout text that comes with every
frame:

```text
Frame at 7.9s (l3:'bucket'+0.8) · scene "limit" 6.1–12.4s · canvas 1080×1920
Visible elements (canvas coordinates):
- limit_title (title, base) box x 60 y 350 w 960 h 220
- tokens (bucket, base) box x 320 y 610 w 440 h 560 · entering
Overlaps between base elements: none
Platform UI zones: none
Caption: A bucket holds five tokens.
```

Read it like a checklist: overlaps marked `(V-8)` must go, any entry under "Platform UI zones" must
move, `entering` means the animation is still running (preview later for the settled layout), and
an empty list means a dead frame.

## Visual QA checklist (per frame)

- Text fits its box: no clipped words, no single orphan word on a line (V-9 catches overflow).
- Nothing overlaps unless it is an overlay meant to (stamp, badge, arrow).
- Nothing in the right rail or under the captions (V-7); 60 px side margins.
- One clear hero; ≤ 3–4 elements visible; the lower half of the stage is not empty by accident.
- The element on screen matches what the caption is saying at that moment.
- Colors carry meaning consistently (red = problem, lime = solution) and text is readable.
- Arabic: captions right-to-left, English terms intact, no broken shaping.

## Render

| Need                                 | MCP (`render_episode`) | CLI                                    |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Preview without a recording          | `silent: true`         | `reelforge render ep10 --silent`       |
| Quick draft                          | `fast: true`           | `--fast`                               |
| Phone or noisy recording             | `denoise: true`        | `--denoise` (or `audio.denoise: true`) |
| Share file size cap (MB, default 28) | `shareMb: 50`          | `--share-size 50`                      |
| Platform layout                      | `preset: reels`        | `--preset tiktok\|reels\|shorts`       |
| No sound effects                     | `sfx: false`           | `--no-sfx`                             |
| A section only                       | (CLI only)             | `--from 12 --to 20` → `<id>.part.mp4`  |

After `render_episode`, poll `get_render_status` every 15–30 s and do other work in between. Do not
start a second render while one runs; `cancel_render` stops it. Never delete the person's files
under `out/`; re-rendering overwrites them.

Outputs in `episodes/<id>/out/`: `<id>.master.mp4` (archive), `<id>.share.mp4` (upload this),
`<id>.srt`, `<id>.sheet.jpg` (contact sheet), `publish.md`.

## Checklist

- [ ] `validate_episode`: 0 errors; warnings fixed or explained to the person.
- [ ] Every scene previewed after its hero entered and at its busiest moment.
- [ ] No overlap, overflow or platform UI hit in any previewed frame (images or layout text).
- [ ] Real cues (aligned or marked), or `silent: true` for a preview render.
- [ ] `meta.publish` filled in: cover, caption, hashtags, pinned.
- [ ] Render polled to completion; output paths reported to the person.

References: [visual-qa](references/visual-qa.md), [render-and-publish](references/render-and-publish.md).

---

<!-- file: skills/reelforge-scene-design/SKILL.md -->

# Design scenes

A scene shows one idea. It starts on a script line (`at: l3`), ends where the next scene starts,
and holds a few elements that enter on the words that name them.

## Stage and safe zones

All `place` coordinates are **stage coordinates**: 1080 wide × 1000 high, origin top-left. The
stage sits between the header and the captions (canvas y 270–1270 on TikTok and Reels, 250–1250 on
Shorts). Platform UI covers parts of the canvas; V-7 warns when an element touches it.

| Rule                        | Value                                          |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Side margins                | `x ≥ 60`, `x + w ≤ 1020`                       |
| Top / bottom breathing room | `y ≥ 40`, `y + h ≤ 960`                        |
| Right rail, lower stage     | below stage y 600: `x + w ≤ 920` (all presets) |
| Main focus area             | stage y 100–800, centered horizontally         |

Per preset (from `presets/*.preset.yaml`, canvas coordinates → stage):

| Preset   | Stage on canvas | Right rail (likes, comments) | In stage coordinates     | Captions at canvas y |
| -------- | --------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------- |
| `tiktok` | y 270–1270      | x ≥ 940 from canvas y 900    | x ≥ 940 from stage y 630 | 1300                 |
| `reels`  | y 270–1270      | x ≥ 960 from canvas y 1000   | x ≥ 960 from stage y 730 | 1290                 |
| `shorts` | y 250–1250      | x ≥ 960 from canvas y 1000   | x ≥ 960 from stage y 750 | 1280                 |

The bottom zones (canvas y ≥ 1500–1560) lie below the stage, under the captions; only
`layout: full` scenes can reach them. Design for TikTok and the layout is safe on all three.

## Hierarchy and density

- **One hero per scene**: the element that carries the idea (title, counter, diagram) takes
  40–70% of the stage.
- **At most 3–4 visible elements at once**, counting arrows and chips. More than that: `exit` the
  old ones or split the scene.
- **Text sizes**: titles 80–130 px and ≤ 7 words; body 36–56 px; labels ≥ 24 px. Nothing smaller
  than 24 px survives a phone screen.
- **Reading order**: top to bottom, in the order things are spoken.
- **Fill the stage**: a lone small element at the top leaves a dead lower half. Center the
  composition vertically or enlarge the hero.
- Base elements must not overlap (V-8, > 15%). Use `layer: overlay` only for stamps, badges and
  arrows that are meant to sit on top.

## Choose a component

| Content         | First choice                                 | Alternatives                                                       |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| One number      | `counter` (big, counts on the number word)   | `stat-card` (with delta), `progress-ring` (percent)                |
| Several numbers | `bar-chart`, `ranking`                       | `donut-chart` (shares), `line-chart` (trend), `table`              |
| A process       | `steps` (3–6 steps)                          | `flow` (pipeline), `cycle` (loop), `lanes` (parallel), `checklist` |
| A comparison    | `comparison` (A vs B rows, winner)           | `before-after`, `table`, `matrix-2x2`, struck `chip`               |
| Places          | `node` boxes + `arrow` with `packet` (route) | `flow` (stops in order), `icon: globe`; `map-route` blueprint      |
| People, roles   | `org-chart`, `quote` (fictional speaker)     | `node` with `icon: user`/`users`, `icon`                           |
| Time            | `timeline` (markers on dates/phases)         | `steps` horizontal, `counter` with a time suffix, `line-chart`     |
| A term or claim | `title` with `**accent**`                    | `chip`, `label`, `stamp` for a verdict                             |
| Code, systems   | `code`, `node` + `arrow`, `grid`, `bucket`   | `phone` for app flows                                              |

Check props with `get_component_schema` before use; the full matrix with sizes is in
[component-matrix](references/component-matrix.md).

## Motion

- Enter **on the word** that names the element: `enter: { at: "l3:'customs'" }`.
- Something enters within the first 1.5 s of every scene (V-11 otherwise).
- Leave ≥ 0.3 s between entrances; the eye follows one thing at a time.
- Vary animations: `reveal` for big titles, `pop`/`spring` for chips and icons, `rise` for cards
  and diagrams, `wipe` for timelines and meters; a `counter` counts by itself from its keyframes.
- Scene transitions: `crossfade` by default, `push` or `zoom` at chapter changes, `cut` for a
  punchline. Camera `drift` or `push-in` on calm scenes, `still` on busy ones.
- At most one `fx` hit (shake, flash, glitch) per scene, on the most important word.

More in [motion](references/motion.md); ready-made coordinates in
[layout-recipes](references/layout-recipes.md).

## Good and bad

Good: a hero and one support element, inside the margins, entering on their words.

```yaml
scenes:
  - id: limit
    at: l4
    glow: cyan
    elements:
      - use: title
        id: limit_title
        props: { text: 'One **bucket** per user' }
        place: { x: 60, y: 80, w: 960, h: 220 }
        enter: { at: "l4:'bucket'", anim: reveal }
      - use: bucket
        id: tokens
        props: { capacity: 5, keyframes: [{ at: "l5:'empty'", tokens: 0 }], rate: '1 token/s' }
        place: { x: 320, y: 340, w: 440, h: 560 }
        enter: { at: "l5:'tokens'", anim: rise }
```

Bad: five elements at once, overlapping boxes, text under the right rail, everything popping at the
scene start.

```yaml
scenes:
  - id: crowded
    at: l4
    elements:
      - {
          use: title,
          props: { text: 'Buckets, tokens, refills, limits and errors' },
          place: { x: 0, y: 0, w: 1080, h: 200 },
        }
      - { use: bucket, props: { capacity: 5 }, place: { x: 100, y: 150, w: 440, h: 560 } }
      - { use: chip, props: { text: '429' }, place: { x: 700, y: 700, w: 340, h: 84 } }
      - { use: node, props: { title: 'API' }, place: { x: 400, y: 300, w: 300, h: 170 } }
      - {
          use: meter,
          props: { keyframes: [{ at: l4, value: 80 }] },
          place: { x: 60, y: 800, w: 1000, h: 180 },
        }
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Every box inside `x 60–1020`, `y 40–960`; lower stage `x + w ≤ 920`.
- [ ] One hero per scene; at most 3–4 visible elements at any moment.
- [ ] Titles ≤ 7 words at 80–130 px; no text below 24 px.
- [ ] Component chosen from the matrix; props checked against the schema.
- [ ] Each element enters on a related word; something enters in the first 1.5 s.
- [ ] No V-6, V-7, V-8 or V-9 warnings; preview frames show no dead half of the stage.

---

<!-- file: skills/reelforge-script-writing/SKILL.md -->

# Write the script

The script is the spine of the video: every scene starts on a line and every element enters on a
word. Write it for the ear first and for captions second.

## Rules

- **Hook in the first 2 seconds.** Line 1 is a question or a surprising fact the viewer cares
  about. The voice must start within 3 s of the recording (V-14 warns after `HOOK_MAX_START` = 3 s).
- **One idea per line.** One spoken sentence, 4–12 words. A line that needs "and" twice is two
  lines.
- **Pace: about 2.3 words per second.** 45 s ≈ 100–110 words; 30 s ≈ 70 words. V-14 warns above
  3.5 words/s (`PACE_MAX_WPS`), measured from a line's cue to the next.
- **Name things on screen.** Put the concrete noun or number that the visual shows in the line
  (`bucket`, `five days`, `customs`): elements enter on those words.
- **Captions:** at most 34 characters per caption line and 2 lines (theme `captions.max_chars`,
  `max_lines`; V-10 warns when a caption wraps more). Short lines caption cleanly; use
  `break: ['word']` to force a break before a word.
- **End with a call to action**: one action (follow, comment a keyword, save), tied to the next
  episode when there is one.
- **Numbers:** say them the way you want them shown; write digits or words consistently, because
  word anchors match the text as written (`l2:'five'` vs `l2:'5'`).

## Structure that works

| Part   | Lines | Job                                            |
| ------ | ----- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Hook   | 1     | Question, surprising number or visible problem |
| Stakes | 1–2   | Why it matters to the viewer                   |
| Core   | 3–7   | The explanation, one step or fact per line     |
| Twist  | 0–2   | The trap, the common mistake or the "but"      |
| Payoff | 1     | The one sentence to remember                   |
| CTA    | 1     | One action, ideally a comment keyword          |

## Good and bad

Good: a hook, one idea per line, concrete nouns to anchor visuals on.

```yaml
script:
  - text: 'Why does a container wait five days at the port?'
  - text: 'Every extra day adds storage fees.'
  - text: 'Most delays come from missing documents.'
  - text: 'Send them before arrival, and it drops to two days.'
  - text: 'Comment SLOTS for part two.'
```

Bad: a slow opener, several ideas per line, too fast to read, no CTA.

```yaml
script:
  - text: 'Hi everyone, welcome back to the channel, today we are going to talk about ports.'
  - text: 'Ports have cranes, customs, trucks, storage yards and documents, and all of them can cause delays depending on many factors.'
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Line 1 is a hook a stranger would stop for; speaking starts within 3 s.
- [ ] Every line holds one idea and 4–12 words; none exceeds 3.5 words/s.
- [ ] Each visual has a word that names it in its line.
- [ ] Captions fit 2 lines of 34 characters (no V-10 warnings).
- [ ] Arabic: technical terms kept in English inside the sentence (`الـ client`).
- [ ] Last line is a single, clear call to action.
- [ ] No real brands, no medical, legal or financial advice (see `reelforge-industry-playbooks`).

References: [arabic](references/arabic.md) (MSA vs dialect, mixed terms) and
[hooks-and-ctas](references/hooks-and-ctas.md) (patterns and examples).

---

<!-- file: skills/reelforge-timing/SKILL.md -->

# Time an episode to the voice

Everything in an episode is timed relative to **cues**: the moment each script line starts in
`voice.wav`. Elements anchor to lines and words, so when the voice changes only the cues move.

## The timing workflow

1. **Before recording**: `draft_cues` (CLI `reelforge cue <id> --draft`) writes estimated cues from
   the text length. The episode previews and validates realistically. V-3 reports
   "draft cues" as info until real cues exist.
2. **After recording**: `align_cues` (CLI `reelforge align <id>`) finds every line and every word in
   `voice.wav` and writes `cues.json` with `auto: true`.
3. **Check by ear**: lines with confidence < 0.5 are listed in the result (`confidence`, and the
   `next` step names them). In the editor's Cues mode they show in **amber**. The person listens
   to those lines and fixes them; you do not guess.
4. **Re-validate**: `validate_episode`. V-14 now measures the real pace (≤ 3.5 words/s) and hook
   start (≤ 3 s), and reports silences ≥ 1.5 s as info.

Engines: `auto` (Whisper when installed, else pause detection), `dsp` (pauses only, instant),
`whisper` (after `reelforge align --setup`, ~180 MB once, offline afterwards). Lines land within
~100 ms; words about 80% of the time within 100 ms.

## Anchor to words, not seconds

| Expression           | Means                           |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `l7`                 | start of line l7                |
| `l7.end`             | start of the next line − 0.15 s |
| `l7:'timeout'`       | first word matching "timeout"   |
| `l7:'request'#2`     | second match in the line        |
| `l7.3`               | 4th word (0-based)              |
| `@hook`, `@hook.end` | a scene's start / end           |
| `…+0.4`, `…-0.2`     | offset in seconds               |
| `12.5s`              | absolute seconds (avoid)        |

Quote expressions containing `:` or `'` in YAML: `at: "l3:'bucket'"`. Use double quotes inside
the expression when the word has an apostrophe: `at: 'l7:"Conway''s"'`. Full rules:
[time-expressions](references/time-expressions.md).

## Good and bad

Good: survives a re-recording.

```yaml
elements:
  - use: stamp
    id: twice
    props: { text: '×2' }
    enter: { at: "l5:'twice'", anim: stamp }
    exit: { at: l6, anim: fade }
```

Bad: breaks as soon as the person speaks faster or slower.

```yaml
elements:
  - use: stamp
    id: twice
    props: { text: '×2' }
    enter: { at: 17.35s, anim: stamp }
    exit: { at: 19s }
```

## Protect hand-marked cues

- `align_cues` refuses to replace cues the person marked by hand unless `force: true`. Do not pass
  `force` without asking.
- Do not edit `cues.json` by hand. Use `set_cues` for known times (`{"l3": 7.42}`), `draft_cues`
  for estimates, `align_cues` for the recording.
- When the voice file changes, V-4 warns: re-run `align_cues` (or ask the person to re-mark).

## Precise hits: word mode

For a stamp or flash that must land exactly on a word, the automatic word time may be up to
~100 ms off. Ask the person to open the editor (`open_editor`), Cues mode, select the line, press
**W** and tap **Space** on each word. Then validate and preview at `"l5:'twice'"`.

## Checklist

- [ ] Draft cues exist before preview; real cues (aligned or marked) before the final render.
- [ ] Every `enter`/`exit`/`fx`/`states` time is a line or word expression, not absolute seconds.
- [ ] Every line with confidence < 0.5 was checked by ear (amber lines in Cues mode).
- [ ] Hand-marked cues were not overwritten (`force` only with permission).
- [ ] No V-2 (unresolvable time), V-3 (missing or out-of-order cues) or V-4 (voice changed).
- [ ] V-14: no line above 3.5 words/s; the hook starts within 3 s.

Reference: [cues-json](references/cues-json.md) (file format, flags and recovery steps).
